studies.finding: Tag/tail/structure manipulations change source-attributed proteasome degradation in lysate, while a stabilized wild-type DHFR domain can persist after terminal-tail clipping.
limitations: These are engineered E. coli DHFR/cpLys38/barnase substrate constructs in rabbit reticulocyte lysate, not a universal survey of naturally damaged proteins or an intact-cell misfolding-surveillance experiment.

Proteasome attribution follows the source lysate assay. No separately purified proteasome, newly isolated E1/E2/E3 requirement, new receptor-binding measurement, ATPase-step assay, translocation movie, force measurement or proteasome-inhibitor control is supplied by the selected main panels.

SDS-PAGE/autoradiography quantifies remaining full-length plus ubiquitinated forms as defined by each panel; His6 immunoblotting localizes loss of a terminal epitope. Band loss, tail clipping, complete destruction and production/reuse of free amino acids are different outcomes.

The source tests folded and methotrexate-stabilized proteins. The assays do not establish that only misfolded proteins are degraded, that native proteins are excluded, or that the proteasome itself decides whether a client is damaged.

The engineered linear Ub4 tag has four N-to-C fused ubiquitin moieties with G76V substitutions. It is not a newly measured native Lys48-isopeptide-linked polyubiquitin chain or an independently observed covalent ubiquitination reaction.

No universal requirement for ubiquitination is admitted; the paper itself cites ubiquitin-independent cases as background. Recognition, initiation, unfolding and proteolysis remain distinct, with the detailed unfolding/pulling cycle conditional.

No raw autoradiograms, numerical rate fit, binding constant, precise substrate concentration or kinetic uncertainty is reconstructed. Exact engineered tail amino-acid sequences are not printed in the reviewed main Methods, and no universal20-residue minimum is admitted from data-not-shown observations.
Selected degradation panels use 25 C and 0.5 mM ATP with regeneration; Figure 1 two-domain direction assays use 30 C and are not silently treated as the same condition.

C-terminal tail effects differ between cpLys38 and wild-type DHFR under 320 micromolar methotrexate: the former can be degraded whereas the latter can be clipped while the stabilized DHFR remains. A tag or tail does not guarantee complete degradation of every substrate.

Tail disorder is a source assignment supported by the paper separate4 C nonspecific-protease sensitivity assay and a hydrodynamic statement partly data-not-shown. It is not a newly solved structure or an independent measurement of every tail conformation.

The ubiquitination control adds2 micromolar Ubal to inhibit deubiquitination and 320 micromolar methotrexate to inhibit degradation. Its accumulating ubiquitin-band signal is a net assay readout under those conditions, not direct matched receptor occupancy or one isolated E1/E2/E3 rate.

Similar source ubiquitination kinetics for full versus shortened N-end-rule tags constrain reduced tagging as the explanation for the deletion effect. They do not prove equal proteasome-binding occupancy or exact chain topology.

The global-unfolding control is a GroEL-binding/protease-protection assay at 15 C with 100 micromolar methotrexate. Degradation uses 25 C and 320 micromolar methotrexate; a similar control trace is not proof of identical local stability or kinetics under every degradation condition.

Nonspecific protease sensitivity and GroEL capture are operational readouts. A similar source global-unfolding trace does not exclude local changes or establish an exact thermodynamic free-energy identity.

studies.observable: Time-resolved35S full-length/ubiquitinated SDS-PAGE bands, fragments and terminal-His6 immunoblot
studies.preparation: Engineer N-end-rule-tagged E. coli DHFR/cpLys38, selected C-terminally tagged cpLys38, lysine-less unstructured-tail additions, terminal His6 and linear Ub4 variants as defined in Figures 2-5. cpLys38 joins the old termini with six glycines and starts at former Lys38/ends at Asn37. The N-end-rule construct first carries a cleavable N-terminal ubiquitin followed by a40-residue lac-repressor-derived linker; lysate cleavage exposes the specified Arg or control Met, with ubiquitin-acceptor Lys15/Lys17 or Arg substitutions. Translate35S-labeled substrates in reticulocyte lysate with 12 mM Arg-Ala for N-end-rule substrates, then centrifuge and ammonium-sulfate partially purify. The His6 immunoblot substrate is separately E. coli-expressed and Ni-NTA purified. Resuspend in 25% glycerol,25 mM MgCl2,0.25 M Tris-HCl pH7.4 and dilute five-fold into ATP-depleted rabbit reticulocyte lysate supplemented with 1 mM DTT,5 mM methionine and 25 micromolar ubiquitin. Prewarm25 C for 3 min; initiate with 0.5 mM ATP,10 mM creatine phosphate and 0.1mg/ml creatine phosphokinase. Compare320 micromolar methotrexate with equal-DMSO controls where indicated. Quench time points into SDS-PAGE buffer and quantify radiolabeled full-length/ubiquitinated bands, fragments and, for the separate purified His6 substrate, terminal-epitope immunoblots.

studies.finding: The selected E. coli enzyme-fraction assay gives DNA- and divalent-ion-dependent labelled CMP incorporation, strongly reduced by the declared component omissions. limitations: An E. coli B enzyme fraction, DNA, nucleotide triphosphates, divalent ions and laboratory buffer are supplied. Purification enrichment does not establish one homogeneous modern RNA-polymerase molecular complex or its subunit mechanism.

The source standard assay is a fixed incubation at 37 C; incorporation is reported as labelled nucleotide in acid-insoluble product. One labelled base does not directly report all incorporated nucleotides without a composition conversion.

Table 2 reports 7.3 millimicromoles CMP incorporation for the complete comparison and less than 0.03 after omitting DNA, enzyme or both divalent cations. These are finite omission results for that preparation, not universal absolute zeroes, microscopic rates or calibrated substrate-count thresholds.

Omission of other triphosphates suppresses the selected CMP assay, but the same publication separately reports ATP-only DNA-dependent polyadenylate formation. Therefore this assay does not prove that all four nucleotide species are universally required for every RNA product or that every DNA-dependent product is a sequence-perfect transcript.

The source product is strongly alkali-sensitive and mostly RNase-sensitive, whereas DNase does not similarly release its label. Residual RNase resistance is unresolved; no complete product sequence, unique initiation/termination mechanism or in-vivo regulatory system is measured.
The source calls supplied DNA a primer; this historical usage is not evidence that a modern covalent primer-dependent initiation mechanism has been identified.

This reconstitution supplies purified mature enzymes and pre-existing phospholipid liposomes; enzymes and substrates are added externally. The source explicitly says this pathway does not support de novo membrane synthesis because PlsB and other components require existing phospholipids/membranes. No first membrane, protein biosynthesis origin, self-reproducing cell or self-made enzyme complement is established.

The selected chemistry context is the three-enzyme PA time course in SI Figure S3. It is distinct from the full eight-enzyme headgroup pathway and the PE/PG endpoint/calibration assays. SI specifies different PlsB/ATP concentrations for that time course than the general main PA procedure; these are retained as different preparations, not silently pooled.

LC-MS records internal-standard-normalized ion counts and source-assigned lipid identities. Species-dependent response, extraction recovery, peak integration and external calibration govern concentration/yield inference. The main text refers to PE/PG standards in Supporting Information, but the retrieved six-page supplement contains no explicit PE/PG calibration curve; no independent absolute-yield or uncertainty reconstruction is made.

Limiting-CoA conversion supports source-specific cofactor recycling, with supplied ATP and substrates. It does not close energy/resource supply, synthesize fatty-acid chains from carbon feedstock, make every phospholipid or show indefinite throughput. Small PA signal without PlsC is source-attributed to possible PlsC contamination of PlsB; omission effects are not treated as perfectly pure single-enzyme controls.

R18 self-quenching is a membrane dye-dilution proxy. In Figure 6 the immediate fluorescence increase follows oleic-acid addition and does not require phospholipid biosynthesis; subsequent PA conversion adds little further fluorescence change. Thus the signal alone cannot isolate synthesis-driven area growth from fatty-acid partition, swelling, fusion or dye redistribution.

The source reports an approximate 25-30 percent expansion from R18 assumptions. No new exact area/volume expansion, vesicle number, leaflet distribution, size distribution or calibrated membrane material balance is independently admitted. Triton-normalized maximal emission is not a direct bilayer surface-area standard.

R18 PA conversion uses 2.7 mM oleic acid and three enzymes. Figure 7 morphology follows a different PG-pathway preparation and a 1.5 mM total fatty-acid feed. These are not matched single-vesicle samples or an interchangeable protocol. Cryo-EM snapshots are not longitudinal lineage/continuous growth tracking.

High-dose material forms stacked multilamellar-like structures that resolve after EDTA. The dosed-feed comparison also lowers magnesium; exact lower magnesium concentration is not resolved in the reviewed main/SI descriptions. Feeding and magnesium are changed together, so an isolated feeding or magnesium causal effect is not established.

The PA-divalent-cation/outer-leaflet imbalance/slow-flip-flop explanation is a source hypothesis. No direct leaflet-resolved synthesis, flip-flop kinetics, cation binding map, complete membrane retention, permeability/selectivity panel, electrochemical gradient or transport activity is measured here.

The title continuous refers to CoA reuse and finite precursor conversion; the conclusion proposes a future continuously controlled feeding system. Finite time courses/endpoints and supplied doses do not demonstrate indefinite membrane production, balanced division, autonomous enzyme renewal or population self-reproduction.
No universal efficiency/robustness benefit, compartmentalized competing metabolism, spontaneous origin sequence, adaptive regulation or required prior metabolic compartment is established.

limitations: The preparation is the developing mouse retinogeniculate system. Engulfment is assayed at P5, segregation at P10/P30 and synaptic puncta at P32-35. Adult maintenance, immune surveillance, disease and all brain regions are not established by these developmental endpoints.

TTX/forskolin are intraocular pharmacological manipulations; CTB labeling follows 4-5 h later. Left-eye drug and right-eye vehicle inputs are compared within selected dLGN regions. Relative labeled-input engulfment is not a direct measurement of every synapse firing rate.

CR3/CD11b and C3 knockouts are developmental whole-animal genotypes. Local attribution to microglia is supported by CR3 expression and absence of other CR3-positive cells in the inspected P5 dLGN; the manipulation is not a microglia-restricted inducible knockout.

Engulfment is reduced, not abolished, in CR3/C3 knockouts. Complement-independent and nonphagocytic mechanisms remain possible. Raw images, complete supplementary methods and the updated supplementary document remain unread; sex is not established by the selected main methods.

limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. No randomized animal allocation, blinded investigation or prospective statistical sample-size calculation is reported. The reporting summary discusses stimulus ordering separately; it does not establish randomized animal groups.

FOS labeling is an activity-associated marker; Vglut2-cre bulk GCaMP6s is a population calcium signal, not a DBH-specific spike recording. Photometry uses saline on day 4 and LPS on day 5 in the same animals. Vagotomized mice form a separate group after two weeks of recovery; a matched abdominal sham is not explicitly specified in the reviewed procedure. Figure 1c reports residual responses after an approximately 80% reduction.

LPS doses differ across assays: 50 micrograms/kg for FOS and TRAP, 0.5 mg/kg for the main photometry comparison, 0.1 mg/kg for cytokine chemogenetics and 12.5 mg/kg for survival. These exposures are not interchangeable. LPS endotoxaemia is distinct from viable bacterial infection.

Descending efferent routes and immune effector cells remain unresolved. A whole-animal Myd88 knockout does not isolate immune-cell-specific mediation. Lower circulating inflammatory cytokines do not imply universally better defense: sustained TRPA1-population activation increased Salmonella tissue burden in the separate live-infection assay.

Raw measurements, animal identifiers and custom code have not been obtained or replayed. Exclusion criteria include unsuccessful targeting/expression/ablation, but counts and operational thresholds are incomplete. Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.
claims.scope: Specified mouse population, intervention, comparator, exposure route and assay window; no universal immune mechanism or clinical efficacy claim.
claims.statement: Peripheral LPS produced more cNST FOS-positive neurons than saline at two hours in the specified counting region. The marker response does not establish DBH-specific firing or identify the peripheral mediator.

limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. No randomized animal allocation, blinded investigation or prospective statistical sample-size calculation is reported. The reporting summary discusses stimulus ordering separately; it does not establish randomized animal groups.

FOS labeling is an activity-associated marker; Vglut2-cre bulk GCaMP6s is a population calcium signal, not a DBH-specific spike recording. Photometry uses saline on day 4 and LPS on day 5 in the same animals. Vagotomized mice form a separate group after two weeks of recovery; a matched abdominal sham is not explicitly specified in the reviewed procedure. Figure 1c reports residual responses after an approximately 80% reduction.

Fos-based TRAP2 labeling is followed by at least four weeks before functional rechallenge to restore LPS sensitivity. LPS-TRAPed, Dbh-cre, Vglut2-cre and Vgat-cre populations are not identical. Dbh expression does not measure norepinephrine release or identify a unique molecular mediator.

Cre-defined nodose activation perturbs marker-defined neurons; it is not selective activation of the TRPA1 channel or CALCA peptide. TRPA1 neurons include different stimulus-responsive subgroups. Extended Data 8e shows two IL-10/fat co-responders among 63 neurons, which the authors did not consider further. Universal zero overlap is unsupported.

Injected cytokines and extraintestinal perfusion have different doses, routes and recording windows. The response classifier uses baseline median absolute deviation, a mean modified z-score above 1.6 and peak fluorescence of at least 1%. Selected, normalized responder heatmaps are not an unbiased full-population distribution. In vivo responses do not establish direct cytokine binding to a neuronal receptor; epithelial or immune intermediates remain possible. Referenced imaging procedures have not been fully audited.

The cNST transcriptomic atlas pools tissue from five animals; 4,008 cells and expression clusters are not independent animal replicates, anatomical coordinates or a measured connectome. Rabies labeling supports an anatomical input interpretation, not synaptic efficacy. Main text calls the rabies reporter dsRed while Methods and Extended Data 12 specify GFP; panel 12d depicts Trpa1 but repeats Calca in its quantitative caption. No tracing fraction is calibrated.

Descending efferent routes and immune effector cells remain unresolved. A whole-animal Myd88 knockout does not isolate immune-cell-specific mediation. Lower circulating inflammatory cytokines do not imply universally better defense: sustained TRPA1-population activation increased Salmonella tissue burden in the separate live-infection assay.

Raw measurements, animal identifiers and custom code have not been obtained or replayed. Exclusion criteria include unsuccessful targeting/expression/ablation, but counts and operational thresholds are incomplete. Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.

The DSS Methods specify CNO in the experimental cohort drinking solution, while Figure 6 says all animals received CNO. Matched control exposure and intake need resolution before a selective DSS mechanism is admitted. This issue does not change the separately described injected-CNO LPS or infection protocols.

NAV-2729 is pharmacological and not exclusively Arf6-selective. Main Methods describe additional GEF/GAP targets in overlapping concentration ranges. PIP2 availability is inferred from kinase and Kir current assays; the study does not directly quantify membrane lipid abundance or test all Arf6 pathways. Focal visual two-photon imaging measures relative diameter; widefield IOS measures an optical HbT-related response. Neither IOS nor the derived response-propagation speed is a calibrated blood-flow, RBC-velocity, oxygen-use or electrical-conduction measurement. General functional analyses select arteries with baseline diameter greater than 15 micrometers.

Visual activity distance uses normalized, thresholded widefield GCaMP, which is biased toward upper cortical layers. The threshold does not prove absence of deeper or sparse activity. Optogenetic distance instead uses a postmortem ChRmine-expression mask, not simultaneous firing measurements. Histological arterial masks are manually registered and refined, not generated causal geometry.

Optogenetic stimulation uses two-second ChRmine pulse trains and six mice per genotype. The zero-laser condition can retain spontaneous vasomotion and imaging-light opsin activation; it is not an opsin-negative control. Functional imaging days 14-16 after viral injection do not specify a universal post-tamoxifen interval.

Propagation velocity is derived from the inverse slope of optical-response onset time versus position along a selected artery, with onset at ten percent of a sigmoid fit. Figure 5E calls it the slope, whereas Methods specify the inverse. Velocity analysis reports thirty averaged repeats, while the general optogenetic protocol reports ninety per power across sessions; subset selection requires clarification.

The manipulation reduces Bax-dependent cell death in the Nestin stem/progenitor lineage; it is not a selective increase in birth rate or a dentate-newborn-neuron-only intervention. Main Figure 2c alternates the order of contexts across days, whereas the discrimination Methods describe training context A followed one hour later by similar context B. The exact per-animal schedule requires reconciliation. The nine-day ratio analysis reports treatment P=0.023; its day F/degree-of-freedom/P combination also needs correction. Handling of a zero sum of freezing scores is unspecified.

Contextual freezing discrimination is a behavioral proxy for pattern separation, not a direct measurement of DG neural population codes or general memory improvement. Supplementary protocol variants have treatment P=0.38 and P=0.06 despite interactions or day-specific differences; they cannot be pooled as uniformly positive main effects.

Supplementary Figure 14 reports an overall discrimination-ratio treatment P=0.1 and interaction P=0.3. Late within-group differences are not a between-group necessity test. Its day-five F(1,14)=4.34/P=0.04 pair needs reconciliation; no replacement biological P value is calculated here.

Dentate localization and absolute cell-number scaling rely on other histological and stereological studies. No human electrical, identified synaptic-output or selective behavioral assay is performed. citations.note: Preparation, scoring and statistical boundaries apply to this finding.

limitations: Adult male C57BL6 YFP-H mice were approximately 2.5-7 months old. Layer 5 neuronal apical tufts were sampled within the superficial 100 micrometers, typically 100-500 micrometers from the posterior-medial infarct edge; this is selected surviving cortex, not the whole injured brain.

Main scientific text, Materials and Methods, and Figures 1-5 with captions are reviewed. Supplemental Figures 1-2 were not obtained or read. Animal-identified image stacks, custom IgorPro routines and the allocation/exclusion manifest were not obtained; no imaging or biological experiment was independently reproduced.

Photothrombosis used Rose Bengal 100 milligrams per kilogram intraperitoneally and 532-nanometer illumination, 17 milliwatts for fifteen minutes, under ketamine-xylazine. Sham controls omitted either dye or illumination. Per-assay sham composition, random allocation and group-specific age distributions are not supplied in the reviewed account.

Imaging under urethane was acute: hourly stacks over six, occasionally seven hours, after a one-, two- or six-week recovery interval, followed by terminal histology. Separate cohorts do not trace the same spine or dendritic arbor continuously from before injury through six weeks.

Only laterally projecting spines were scored. New spines had to protrude at least four pixels, approximately 0.55 micrometers, and remain present at the six-hour endpoint. Transient events, filopodium conversions, shifted segments and poor-quality images were excluded. The assay is not a census of all spine births, losses or synapses.

Turnover is reported as a percentage of the counted spine population over the imaging session; raw animal-level numerator/denominator assignments are unavailable. Spine density is a count per ten micrometers of dendrite. Neither measure is a neuron birth rate, a universal hourly turnover constant or a calibrated graph weight.

Turnover scoring was blinded to experimental condition, but movement, abnormal breathing and image deterioration could exclude experiments; exclusion counts and animal identifiers are not supplied. Axial optical resolution was about 5.3 micrometers, much poorer than lateral resolution, and six spine-appearance cases were pooled across animals for shaft-fluorescence controls.

Spine morphology and adjacent sensory-evoked reflectance do not measure the functional efficacy of each new synapse, selective memory content or behavioral recovery. The Discussion explicitly leaves the causal link between increased formation and recovered function unestablished.

The main text gives a 0.14 percent control formation mean and 1.37, 0.93 and 0.75 percent poststroke means. The abstract describes a five- to eight-fold peak increase; these rounded quantities do not define one exact fold estimate. Retain the reported assay means without calibrating a universal multiplier.

Nonsignificant outcomes are not equivalence or full recovery. Photothrombosis does not permit controlled reperfusion, and the paper does not directly establish the same time course in other stroke models, traumatic injury or humans.
claims.scope: The stated mouse preparation, anatomical sample, recovery interval, acute imaging window and comparator; no universal injury prerequisite, neuron birth claim or quantitative graph weight.
claims.statement: At one week after photothrombosis, the reported six-hour spine-formation percentage was 1.37, versus 0.14 in controls; 4 poststroke mice and six controls. The increase concerns retained new lateral protrusions in the sampled peri-infarct cortex, not continuous weeks-long tracking or neuronal birth.

Global neuronal 2POP fitting reports a renewing fraction near 0.35, with a reported 95% interval of 0.12-0.63. For nonneuronal cells the main text reports 0.51 with interval 0.22-0.88, accepted Table S2 gives 0.56, and individual fits fix 0.55. These summaries must not be treated as one exactly reproduced estimate.

The reported individual medians, 1.75% per year for neurons and 3.5% for nonneuronal cells, apply within fixed renewing fractions of 0.35 and 0.55 after the stated exclusions. Global-fit rates of about 12% and 4.9% per year in Tables S3 and S2 are different estimands. Unfittable samples were excluded from the individual 2POP analysis; Figure 2C/5A additionally states plot limits below 0.001 or above 1.5.

The accepted supplement distinguishes unpaired 2POP comparison (51 neuronal and 64 nonneuronal fractions, rank-sum P=0.005) from 40 matched pairs (signed-rank P=0.054; neuronal median 1.5%, nonneuronal 3.5% per year). The latter null does not establish equal rates. Comparing these tests without their populations and denominators would be misleading.

Age associations use cross-sectional, model-derived rates: reported neuronal r=-0.31, P=0.03 and nonneuronal r=-0.35, P=0.04. They do not trace the same people over time or identify an age intervention. The sex comparison P=0.41 does not establish equivalence. The DCX overlay uses an external Knoth cohort, not birthdating of the same cells.

The accepted supplement prints a heuristic labeled AIC, p + log2(SSE), and requires a halving of SSE per added parameter. Applying that printed rule to rounded Table S2 gives 0.31 > 0.51/2, so its nonneuronal 2POP preference does not follow from that rule. Table S3 has 0.17 < 0.49/2 for neurons. This arithmetic checks reporting consistency only; final supplementary methods, likelihood and code remain unverified.

The source says subjects born around 1955-1965 discriminate 2POP from homogeneous age-dependent alternatives; without them the scenarios could not be distinguished. MCMC explores bounded parameter sets, and fitting several scenarios does not prove a unique biological mechanism. Full numerical replay and out-of-sample discrimination have not been performed.

The fitting procedure assumes a one-year food lag and development beginning six months before birth. Its weighted SSE squares weights of 1 or 2 assigned around a 10-microgram carbon boundary. Table S1 has both estimated DNA carbon mass and reactor-measured mass, including ND entries. The exact mass choice, boundary treatment and missing-value policy require executable code before reproducing the fit.

The supplement explicitly does not explore population feedback: birth and death rates do not depend on the population state. Constant population size in replacement scenarios is imposed by their birth boundary, not observed emergence of a stabilizing rule. Population turnover does not identify one-for-one functional replacement, circuit topology or a universal minimal assembly.

The approximately 700 neurons per day in each hippocampus and 0.004% of dentate neurons per day are model-dependent estimates, not directly counted daily births.

The source says subjects born around 1955-1965 discriminate 2POP from homogeneous age-dependent alternatives; without them the scenarios could not be distinguished. MCMC explores bounded parameter sets, and fitting several scenarios does not prove a unique biological mechanism. Full numerical replay and out-of-sample discrimination have not been performed.

The fitting procedure assumes a one-year food lag and development beginning six months before birth. Its weighted SSE squares weights of 1 or 2 assigned around a 10-microgram carbon boundary. Table S1 has both estimated DNA carbon mass and reactor-measured mass, including ND entries. The exact mass choice, boundary treatment and missing-value policy require executable code before reproducing the fit.

Figure 6 illustrates 2POPEd with initial renewing fraction 0.31, nonrenewing death rate 0.0035 per year, newborn death rate 0.11 per year and death-rate half-reduction age 19 years. The chosen set belongs to the best 3% of 300,000 explored sets; it is not a uniquely identified law. The reported 7.1-year half-life and external stereological age profiles are model-linked summaries, not longitudinal tracking of those human neurons.

The supplement explicitly does not explore population feedback: birth and death rates do not depend on the population state. Similar estimated rates across species do not supply human functional integration or a birth-to-cognition mechanism. Histology, isotope dating, molecular markers and rodent interventions remain distinct evidence.

Repeated exposures and long retention windows are not independent animals or instantaneous birth rates.

Table 1 describes six-digit dates as day/month/year, although entries such as 013183 require month/day/year. limitations: Social isolation starts immediately after weaning and lasts at least six weeks before labeling. The two housing conditions are crossed with light versus sham; this is not a selective learning manipulation. PV activity and extracellular GABA are not measured as the intervening response to isolation in the same animals.

Population experiments use five consecutive days of stimulation, eight hours per day: ChR2 blue light at 472 nm, 5-ms pulses at 8 Hz for 30 seconds every five minutes, or continuous 593-nm eNpHR light. AAV volume, delivered light power and a full opsin-negative illumination control are not reported. No-light sham comparisons include the effects of the complete light protocol.

On day five, EdU is injected intraperitoneally at 41.1 mg/kg six times, two hours apart, with collection two hours after the last injection. Repeated injections are not independent replicates. EdU incorporation and MCM2 expression are cycle-related endpoints, not counts of completed neuronal differentiation, integrated neurons or an instantaneous birth rate.

Population scoring uses 40-micrometre sections, every sixth section, and nestin-positive inverted-Y morphology over an EdU- or MCM2-positive nucleus. Optogenetic counts are limited to one millimetre anterior and posterior to the injection. Densities per cubic millimetre and the MCM2-positive fraction have distinct denominators. Analyses are described as blinded; random assignment, raw unit records and multiplicity-adjusted tests are not supplied.

The 2026 comparison has independently recomputed deposited readouts and a selected offline check. Layer mixing affects several joint fits, but the leading DINOv3-small plus description result remains. Network inference and minimum-program search are not reproduced; the fits do not identify a human generative mechanism.

Wang et al. spatial fMRI contrasts are observational neural readouts under a task. The publication explicitly lacks temporal resolution to identify its proposed nested code; anatomical ordering does not establish a top-down construction pathway.

Al Roumi et al. 2023 compares a chosen binary repetition language with a limited set of models; Alternate bracketing is an exception. Its neural violation classifier does not decode a full program or establish the proposed prefrontal prediction pathway.

limitations: The fit uses selected sequences and group error profiles, with fixed capacity Kmax=12 and chosen noise assumptions. Fitted probabilities combine within-person nonuse and between-person variation; they are not measured fractions of people lacking a resource. No held-out task or neural carrier test is reported.

The printed implementation is not unambiguous: S1 Text gives three repetitions of a two-output program an eight-output example; with binary logarithms its listed Repeat+1 program costs 7 while the figure labels K=5. Main-text 2points/4points costs are 6/9, whereas S1 Figure 2 labels 7/11. The formula, initial-state convention and program inventory require reconciliation before exact minima are admitted.

The reduced-resource description sets disallowed program costs to 12 while the stated threshold admits costs at most 12. Prefix correction, random-choice indexing and selection among programs versus sequences also require reconciliation. Published plots alone do not resolve these choices.

The 2021 MEG supplement repeats the cost-5 repeat description and lists an initial output followed by four pairs for alternate and two-crosses sequences. These descriptions require consistent output-length and cost conventions before executable or minimum-program claims.

Wang et al. (2019) uses alternating two-step and opposing one-step rotations, while Al Roumi et al. (2021) uses three-step and opposing one-step rotations under the same alternate name. Two-crosses is treated as three-level in 2019 and non-nested in the 2021 table. Template identity and parse must be explicit; names do not determine a shared structure.

limitations: The abstract's four macrocomponents and the body's three grouped components are different groupings of the proposed architecture. Neither yields a measured carrier count, calibrated dependency weight or validated graph-generation rule. A selective causal assay must define whether its outcome is recognition, felt sharing, perspective taking or helping.

Perceptual access to social information does not establish one universal visual or multisensory mechanism. The review includes observed, imagined and narrated situations; no selective test makes one perception node necessary for all of them.

Affective sharing is part of this attributed definition, but a definition does not prove a necessary dependency on every affect-generation process. Recognition, concern, personal distress, felt sharing and helping are different outcomes.

Working memory, inhibitory control and mentalizing are not interchangeable. Pages 82 and 86 describe dissociations between executive-task and theory-of-mind impairments; these secondary summaries require primary review before any specific lesion effect is admitted. They do not calibrate a universal maintenance dependency.

Page 91 states that the proposed psychological constructs are not primitive and still need decomposition. There is no fixed cardinality, measured carrier threshold or numerical weighting of perception, affect and control. Frontal activation can reflect inhibition or monitoring/manipulation of internally generated information; neither is uniquely established by the review.

limitations: The production data are from trapdoor-loaded UCN in 2020, 2021 and 2022. This paper reports a 45 cm/about 45 neV trap depth and cleaning at 38 cm; those numbers must not silently replace the different 2017/2018 preparation description.

Roundhouse-dump normalization and a second, energy-sensitive monitor reduce sensitivity to the loaded spectrum; they do not make its distribution identical to the stored population. Short-hold data fit spectral and rolling normalization corrections.

Coincidences begin with two PMTs within 100 ns, extend until a gap above 1000 ns and use a 20 ns fixed dead time; the standard threshold is ten photons. Detector-live-time and photon-tail/pileup corrections are fitted or simulated, not independently replayed here.

About 90% of production runs pass analyzer-dependent selection. At least three analyses per year share the acquisitions. Final selection must not be described as entirely blinded.

DQE parameters are adjusted from short-hold fluctuations and fit quality; reduced chi-square one is partly imposed, not an independent validation of the noise model.

Rolling normalization uses short holds in overlapping blocks, typically fifteen runs within epochs. Its covariance and uncertainty are not independently reconstructed by dividing a printed yield error by the fitted correction factor.

limitations: QED_L removes spatial photon zero modes on every time slice. QED_TL removes only the four-momentum zero mode and has an ill-defined T-to-infinity limit at fixed L for the conventional charged-particle mass extraction. This is a regulator distinction, not two experimental forces.

At order alpha, the leading mass correction is -q^2*alpha*kappa/(2*L)*(1+2/(m*L)), with kappa approximately 2.837297 in units hbar=c=1. Universality through 1/L^2 assumes the photon is the only massless asymptotic state and the charged particle is stable and nondegenerate with states sharing its quantum numbers.

Terms of order 1/L^3 can depend on internal structure and spin; a point-fermion coefficient cannot be imposed on every hadron. Vanishing leading q^2 terms for a neutral particle do not prove absence of all finite-volume effects.

In the full QCD+QED theory the paper's continuum prescription retains an extremely small nonzero cutoff because of QED triviality. Its practical extrapolation does not establish a nonperturbative interacting QED limit at exactly zero lattice spacing.

limitations: These four runs are a subset of the 14 charged production ensembles, not an independent replication of the 41-ensemble result. The temporal extent changes with the spatial box and the QED_L large-time assumptions remain applicable.

The bare coupling e=1.00 is larger than the physical coupling. Figure 1 uses the approximate label bare alpha about 1/10; e^2/(4*pi), the renormalized flow coupling and physical alpha are distinct quantities.
The plotted kaon mass-squared difference is negative at this enhanced coupling. That sign is not the physical kaon mass ordering and is not evidence of a neutron-proton sign reversal.

No significant neutral-kaon volume dependence is resolved in this scan; that does not prove exactly zero corrections. The charged-neutral difference needs a fitted 1/L^3 term in addition to the universal leading terms.

These are reported computational results for the specified action, ensembles and fitting procedure. The 60 TB archive, correlators, covariance matrices and analysis code have not been independently replayed.

QED_L removes spatial photon zero modes on every time slice. QED_TL removes only the four-momentum zero mode and has an ill-defined T-to-infinity limit at fixed L for the conventional charged-particle mass extraction. This is a regulator distinction, not two experimental forces.

At order alpha, the leading mass correction is -q^2*alpha*kappa/(2*L)*(1+2/(m*L)), with kappa approximately 2.837297 in units hbar=c=1. Universality through 1/L^2 assumes the photon is the only massless asymptotic state and the charged particle is stable and nondegenerate with states sharing its quantum numbers.

Terms of order 1/L^3 can depend on internal structure and spin; a point-fermion coefficient cannot be imposed on every hadron. Vanishing leading q^2 terms for a neutral particle do not prove absence of all finite-volume effects.

In the full QCD+QED theory the paper's continuum prescription retains an extremely small nonzero cutoff because of QED triviality. Its practical extrapolation does not establish a nonperturbative interacting QED limit at exactly zero lattice spacing.

limitations: The primary physical-point inputs are M_pi+=139.570, M_K+=493.68, M_K0=497.61, M_D0=1864.9 and M_Omega=1672.4 MeV, with alpha^-1=137.036. The kaon squared-mass input is 3896 MeV^2. These are the paper's adopted inputs, not independent mass measurements or predictions reproduced here.

Omega sets the final scale. The exploratory w0=0.1755 fm value and charmonium tuning target are preparation aids, not extra predicted observables. The ratio and mass-independent normalization methods reuse the same ensembles.
Equation S37 uses the kaon squared-mass difference, which itself mixes QCD and QED. Its second term is not a pure strong contribution before a separation convention is supplied.

The alternative analysis using the Sigma splitting in place of the kaon difference has a different input set; a quantity used to tune that alternative cannot simultaneously count as its independent prediction.

The Wilson-flow charge is defined at hadronic scales, with final choices 280 and 525 MeV. Matching to the Thomson-limit input neglects effects of order alpha^2 at the stated precision; bare e is not the renormalized physical coupling.
About 500 fit variants vary normalization, mass dependence, cutoff terms, two correlator starts and two charge-renormalization scales. They reuse simulation data and are not independent replications.

AIC weights are proportional to exp[-(chi^2+2*p)/2]. The weighted mean gives the central estimate, variation among fits estimates systematic uncertainty, and the complete procedure is repeated on 2000 bootstrap samples for statistical uncertainty. AIC weights are not probabilities of physical truth or graph-edge strengths.

The chosen family includes g^2*a or a^2 discretization terms, mass extrapolations, and a fitted 1/L^3 electromagnetic term after the leading finite-volume corrections. Its uncertainty does not exhaust arbitrary omitted models or higher orders.
The primary Coleman-Glashow combination is fitted rather than constrained to zero. One auxiliary cross-check assumes that relation; it cannot independently verify the relation it imposes.

Three auxiliary analyses reuse the data; details are not fully supplied. One masks mass differences by a random factor between 0.7 and 1.3. This is not independent simulation replication or evidence that every analysis was blinded.

The neutron-proton total is reported as about five standard deviations above zero under the selected error construction. The paper does not supply an independently reproduced discovery p-value here. Comparisons with known masses are postdictions; the 2015 statement that some channels were unmeasured is not a current experimental census.

These are reported computational results for the specified action, ensembles and fitting procedure. The 60 TB archive, correlators, covariance matrices and analysis code have not been independently replayed.

Stability in this calculation concerns the included strong and electromagnetic interactions. Weak decays, a neutron lifetime, proton-decay bounds, nuclear stability and real-time hadron formation are outside its calculated scope.

Quark flavors, field components, sources per configuration and fitted states are different counting domains. The calculation establishes no universal constituent minimum or graph-level generative rule.

Table parentheses apply to the last digits. The Coleman-Glashow combination is separately fitted with correlations; neither exact cancellation nor its uncertainty follows from adding the independently rounded marginal table entries.

limitations: The five configuration groups are combined as two campaign sets because settings within a campaign share an angle calibration. They are not five independent mass experiments.
Each angle determination uses four profiles in the +,-,-,+ sequence. Bragg-angle counts, scan points, detected photons and independent calibration sets are distinct counting domains.

Profiles contain approximately 45 points with 60 or 90 seconds per point. A scan-specific summed pulse-height window precedes fitting dynamical diffraction profiles with Gaussian broadening; a profile width is not a direct neutron mass.

The approximately 6 g Kapton source in three graphite holders is exposed to about 5e14 neutrons per square centimeter per second. Its roughly 450 C environment and about 1.2 percent daily hydrogen loss do not describe isolated stationary free neutrons.

Four optical-polygon calibrations near the campaigns use the sum of 24 exterior angles, 2*pi. One serves 1995 and three serve March 1998; the 1998 humidity dependence is about 0.5e-6 per ten percentage points, with calibration relative uncertainty expanded to 1e-7.

Within each campaign the weighted-mean uncertainty is enlarged by sqrt(chi^2/dof), then the 1e-7 relative calibration uncertainty is added in quadrature. The two campaign means are combined before adding crystal-temperature and vertical-divergence contributions.

limitations: PNP detects the ion after coherent radial-to-axial transfer. Its resonant voltages differ for N+ and N2+, changing equilibrium position in stray fields. The SOF protocol keeps the evolution voltage common and changes it only for detection.

limitations: The stored ions are measured alternately under the same trap voltages, using separate axial resonators. Randomized species order reduces linear drift; it does not make sequential measurements simultaneous or statistically independent.
The proton dataset comprises thirteen runs and three ion pairs, with about 300 hours of acquisition over two months. Runs, cycles, ion pairs and publications are not independent replications.
The planar fit extrapolates the deliberately excited cyclotron motion to zero using R_i=R_stat+a*S_p^2+b*S_C^2. Thermal axial and cyclotron motion still requires systematic corrections.
The 2019 reanalysis corrects the estimated ion temperatures and a minor measurement-program flaw in the 2017 datasets. The two publications cannot be averaged as independent proton-mass experiments.

Heiße 2017 Figure 3 lists phase-unwrapping times 0.1, 1, 2 and 5 s; Heiße 2019 describes 0.5, 1, 2 and 5 s. The four final 10 s phase evolutions are distinct from those unwrapping stages; the differing descriptions are retained.

The 2017 abbreviation MT denotes the measurement trap; in 2019 PT denotes the precision trap and MT the magnetometer trap. The proposed simultaneous three-ion readout and magnetic shim coils were not used in the reported proton campaign.

The proton campaign had C4=(0 +/- 6.3)e-6 and C6=(-6.8 +/- 0.4)e-4. The improved Table VI tuning and proposed millikelvin cooling describe other conditions, not the acquisition used for the reported mass.

Table VII revises feedback-cooled axial temperatures to 1.5(1.0) K for p and 4.5(1.4) K for C-12(6+), replacing the 2017 common 1.7(1.0) K estimate. No-feedback values are 3.4(1.0) K and 6.4(1.0) K. These are inferred temperatures, not zero thermal energies.
The reanalysis uses B2=-0.270(15) microtesla/mm^2. Reduced chi-square 1.17 for ten degrees of freedom and a 30 percent tail do not logically exclude common systematic effects.

limitations: COMSOL 5.2 with the AC/DC module represents a point charge and perfectly conducting grounded electrode surfaces. Twenty-one ion positions from -0.5 to +0.5 mm are fitted with odd polynomials to extract field gradients.

The cylinder reference, polynomial order and matrix-truncation checks constrain numerical error. Increasing resolution or expansion order alone does not prove convergence or exact reproduction of the manufactured trap.

limitations: Schuh uses 120 cycles over 23 days, with 73 cycles at 40 s and the others at 20 s, and approximately 140 minutes per full cycle. Two 4.6 ms magnetron pulses and an intentionally deformed readout potential distinguish this experiment from proton-mass PnA acquisition.

The readout uses C2=-0.5997, C4=-0.00223(18), C6=0.014(4) and a maximal magnetron radius near 274 micrometers. Harmonic potential during phase evolution and deformed potential during readout must not be conflated.

The 43 microhertz statistical error is enlarged by sqrt(2) to 61 microhertz because the reduced chi-square is 2. Tilt fluctuations cannot be separated from voltage fluctuations by the axial signal alone.

The image-charge difference subtracts ideal 390.723(1) mHz, magnetic 0.056(21) mHz and tilt/ellipticity 0.188(37) mHz from 393.258(61)(77) mHz. The resulting 2.291(61)(111) mHz combines correlated correction uncertainties.

The 73 and 37 microhertz tilt contributions are correlated and add to 110 microhertz. The two 21 microhertz magnetic contributions cancel in the stated analysis; quadrature of all marginal errors would misrepresent that covariance.

Appendix A uses the 2017 proton mass and compares an axial calibration ratio over 1000 measurements drawn from both the image-charge and proton campaigns. This shared input prevents a claim of fully independent proton-mass validation.

The page 6 prose labels a ratio of magnetron frequencies as axial; Appendix A explicitly defines the required ratio using nu_z. The calibration follows the axial observable and retains the printed discrepancy.

For ion charge n*e, Schuh 2019 defines radial actual-minus-ideal shifts Delta_nu_plus/minus=opposite-sign n*E_rho/(2*pi*B0). The correction added to the measured cyclotron estimate is +n*(2*E_rho+E_z)/(4*pi*B0), in Hz. The change of sign convention is explicit in footnote 2.

The infinitely long cylindrical-electrode approximation gives a relative cyclotron correction approximately m/(4*pi*epsilon0*B0^2*rho0^3). Real gaps, electrode shape, displacements and axial fields require a scoped geometry calculation.

The invariance-based cyclotron estimate retains an image-charge correction. Cancellation of the opposite radial shifts in nu_plus+nu_minus does not establish that the squared-frequency reconstruction is unshifted.

limitations: Neutral carbon-12 has mass exactly 12 u; C-12(6+) instead has mass 12 u minus six electron masses plus the six positive ionization energies divided by c^2. The sixfold charge factor in m_p=R*m_C/6 cannot be omitted.

Heiße 2019 uses m_e=0.000548579909069(15) u and historical electronic-energy inputs. The electron mass is inferred using a bound-electron g factor and QED; it is not an independently reproduced direct weighing in this review.

Heiße 2017 prints m_C=11.9967096264139(10) u and 0.08 ppt relative uncertainty. Heiße 2019 prints 11.99670962641385(8) u but still states 0.08 ppt; the printed (8) corresponds to about 0.00667 ppt. This unresolved uncertainty discrepancy is not silently repaired.

The proton-electron ratio in Heiße 2019 assumes zero covariance because the dominant proton and electron systematic uncertainties differ. That assumption is not proof of complete statistical independence.

The stored ions are measured alternately under the same trap voltages, using separate axial resonators. Randomized species order reduces linear drift; it does not make sequential measurements simultaneous or statistically independent.
The proton dataset comprises thirteen runs and three ion pairs, with about 300 hours of acquisition over two months. Runs, cycles, ion pairs and publications are not independent replications.
The planar fit extrapolates the deliberately excited cyclotron motion to zero using R_i=R_stat+a*S_p^2+b*S_C^2. Thermal axial and cyclotron motion still requires systematic corrections.
The 2019 reanalysis corrects the estimated ion temperatures and a minor measurement-program flaw in the 2017 datasets. The two publications cannot be averaged as independent proton-mass experiments.

Heiße 2017 Figure 3 lists phase-unwrapping times 0.1, 1, 2 and 5 s; Heiße 2019 describes 0.5, 1, 2 and 5 s. The four final 10 s phase evolutions are distinct from those unwrapping stages; the differing descriptions are retained.

The 2017 abbreviation MT denotes the measurement trap; in 2019 PT denotes the precision trap and MT the magnetometer trap. The proposed simultaneous three-ion readout and magnetic shim coils were not used in the reported proton campaign.

The proton campaign had C4=(0 +/- 6.3)e-6 and C6=(-6.8 +/- 0.4)e-4. The improved Table VI tuning and proposed millikelvin cooling describe other conditions, not the acquisition used for the reported mass.

Heiße 2019 Table VIII reports corrections in parts per trillion: image charge 91.0(4.6), image current -1.9(0.3), line shape 3.1(3.0), magnetron determination 0.0(0.6), magnetic inhomogeneity -20.9(27.4), relativity -8.9(7.1), and electrostatic terms much smaller than 0.1. Its total is 59.5(28.8).

Adding all finite displayed rows gives 62.4 ppt. The line-shape correction varies by ion pair; the 2017 Table I caption explicitly excludes its pair-specific term from that earlier total. Omitting the 2019 line-shape row gives 59.3 ppt. The final weighting and application to the reanalysis have not been reconstructed; a naive sum is not evidence that the mass result is invalid.

The 2019 Table VIII header is (R_stat-R_cor)/R_stat, but Equations 20 and 23 increase R, giving (R_cor-R_stat)/R_stat about +59.55 ppt from rounded values. The printed sign convention remains unresolved.

Table VII revises feedback-cooled axial temperatures to 1.5(1.0) K for p and 4.5(1.4) K for C-12(6+), replacing the 2017 common 1.7(1.0) K estimate. No-feedback values are 3.4(1.0) K and 6.4(1.0) K. These are inferred temperatures, not zero thermal energies.
The reanalysis uses B2=-0.270(15) microtesla/mm^2. Reduced chi-square 1.17 for ten degrees of freedom and a 30 percent tail do not logically exclude common systematic effects.

Heiße 2019 Equation 21 prints a frequency shift with a dimensionless right side; the relative form in Heiße 2017 Equation 2 and the explicit conventions in Schuh 2019 are used instead. The positive E/(m*c^2) beside a negative relativistic shift on page 13 is not adopted as a physical identity.
For positive deuteron binding energy, m_n=m_d-m_p+E_B/c^2. The subtraction wording on Heiße 2019 page 14 is not an independent neutron-mass determination or a replacement for that mass balance.
These are reported measurements or calculations with scoped interpretations. Original acquisition records, analysis code, thermal corrections and full covariance have not been independently replayed.

limitations: Schuh uses 120 cycles over 23 days, with 73 cycles at 40 s and the others at 20 s, and approximately 140 minutes per full cycle. Two 4.6 ms magnetron pulses and an intentionally deformed readout potential distinguish this experiment from proton-mass PnA acquisition.

The readout uses C2=-0.5997, C4=-0.00223(18), C6=0.014(4) and a maximal magnetron radius near 274 micrometers. Harmonic potential during phase evolution and deformed potential during readout must not be conflated.

The 43 microhertz statistical error is enlarged by sqrt(2) to 61 microhertz because the reduced chi-square is 2. Tilt fluctuations cannot be separated from voltage fluctuations by the axial signal alone.

The image-charge difference subtracts ideal 390.723(1) mHz, magnetic 0.056(21) mHz and tilt/ellipticity 0.188(37) mHz from 393.258(61)(77) mHz. The resulting 2.291(61)(111) mHz combines correlated correction uncertainties.

The 73 and 37 microhertz tilt contributions are correlated and add to 110 microhertz. The two 21 microhertz magnetic contributions cancel in the stated analysis; quadrature of all marginal errors would misrepresent that covariance.

Appendix A uses the 2017 proton mass and compares an axial calibration ratio over 1000 measurements drawn from both the image-charge and proton campaigns. This shared input prevents a claim of fully independent proton-mass validation.

The page 6 prose labels a ratio of magnetron frequencies as axial; Appendix A explicitly defines the required ratio using nu_z. The calibration follows the axial observable and retains the printed discrepancy.

limitations: COMSOL 5.2 with the AC/DC module represents a point charge and perfectly conducting grounded electrode surfaces. Twenty-one ion positions from -0.5 to +0.5 mm are fitted with odd polynomials to extract field gradients.

Agreement between finite-element and semianalytical calculations is tested on the same simplified geometry. Full electrode geometry changes the LIONTRAP correction by 2.7(4) percent; horizontal and azimuthal slit effects are separately reported.

Numerical/fit and geometry uncertainties have different meanings. The geometry estimate assumes manufacturing deviations up to 10 micrometers; higher-order effects are treated as small under a displacement assumption below 50 micrometers.

The cylinder reference, polynomial order and matrix-truncation checks constrain numerical error. Increasing resolution or expansion order alone does not prove convergence or exact reproduction of the manufactured trap.

The calculation and experiment have shared geometry and calibration assumptions. Their agreement is conditional evidence for an image-charge correction in the stated trap, not a universal graph-generation rule or an independent mass measurement.

For ion charge n*e, Schuh 2019 defines radial actual-minus-ideal shifts Delta_nu_plus/minus=opposite-sign n*E_rho/(2*pi*B0). The correction added to the measured cyclotron estimate is +n*(2*E_rho+E_z)/(4*pi*B0), in Hz. The change of sign convention is explicit in footnote 2.

The infinitely long cylindrical-electrode approximation gives a relative cyclotron correction approximately m/(4*pi*epsilon0*B0^2*rho0^3). Real gaps, electrode shape, displacements and axial fields require a scoped geometry calculation.

The invariance-based cyclotron estimate retains an image-charge correction. Cancellation of the opposite radial shifts in nu_plus+nu_minus does not establish that the squared-frequency reconstruction is unshifted.

limitations: COMSOL 5.2 with the AC/DC module represents a point charge and perfectly conducting grounded electrode surfaces. Twenty-one ion positions from -0.5 to +0.5 mm are fitted with odd polynomials to extract field gradients.

The cylinder reference, polynomial order and matrix-truncation checks constrain numerical error. Increasing resolution or expansion order alone does not prove convergence or exact reproduction of the manufactured trap.

limitations: The 2021 FSU experiment measures both ions simultaneously in coupled magnetron orbits. It is distinct from the 2020 alternation between a central ion and a 2 mm parked ion.

At 8.5 T the separation radius is 0.79-0.82 mm and the common-mode radius is below 0.03 mm. Orbits about 0.4 mm from the central gas beam improve collision survival; this is not an intrinsic molecular lifetime.

Cooling is alternating on the detector resonance, but PnP phase readout is simultaneous. Phase fits and the cited Thompson thesis equations convert trap-modified frequencies to the free ratio; those upstream equations and raw phases are not independently replayed.
Field-noise rejection is not total-uncertainty reduction. Thermal relativistic noise remains and the reported gain per mass-2 run is only slightly above a factor of two.
The usual 5 ms cyclotron drive produces about 21 micrometers of motion. Fits versus drive time squared extrapolate the driven contribution; 6 ms data are excluded from the final correction estimates.

Zero drive does not remove thermal imbalance. The 2.9(2.9) correction in absolute ratio units of 1e-12 comes from a phase-noise diagnostic with 100 percent assigned uncertainty, equivalent to a 0.66 K axial-temperature difference.

Table I corrections in absolute ratio units of 1e-12 are 29.5(1.4), 2.9(2.9), ion-ion <0.1, -1.1(0.2) and +0.5(0.5), with total 31.8(3.7). Naive independent quadrature of the listed nonzero errors gives about 3.265, not 3.7. Full covariance and rounding details are unavailable; no erroneous published uncertainty is established.

limitations: No statistically significant excess in these two selected channels does not establish eternal proton stability, absence of every decay channel, neutron stability, nucleon formation or universal constituent minima.

The April 1996-May 2018 SK-I-IV acquisition is shared by both channel searches. The enlarged fiducial mass is 27.2 kton: 22.5 conventional plus 4.7 additional. The paper reports nominal 450 kton-years, including earlier 306 kton-years and 144 newly analyzed; this is not an independent replication of the earlier search.

Conventional vertices have dwall>200 cm; additional vertices have 100<dwall<=200 cm. The outside region 50<dwall<=100 cm is excluded. The eye scan informed selection changes; no event was rejected solely by scanning.

Selection C1-C8 requires fully contained events, two or three rings, channel-specific showering and Michel-electron tags, a three-ring pion mass of 85-185 MeV/c^2, total mass 800-1050 MeV/c^2 and total momentum below 250 MeV/c. Only SK-IV additionally requires no tagged neutron.

The SK-IV neutron tag uses a 2.2 MeV hydrogen-capture gamma, hits in 18-535 microseconds and a trained classifier. Its estimated efficiency is 25.2+/-2.3 percent with 0.018 false positives per primary event; no tag is not proof that no neutron was emitted.

The surviving muon-channel candidate is the earlier SK-IV upper-momentum conventional-volume candidate. A second earlier candidate moved outside the signal region after recalibration; changed selection does not create an independent acquisition.

limitations: The ideal transfer identity uses R_Pu=r_Pu,stack/Omega_stack, Omega_AG=r_Pu,AG/R_Pu and R_n=r_gamma,thick*r_alpha,thin/(r_gamma,thin*Omega_AG). The boron gamma branching fraction and thin-target absorption normalization cancel only with the stated common detector response and loss corrections. Omega here is a fraction of 4*pi; illuminated alpha-detector area is assumed fully efficient. R_Pu denotes total alpha emission from the source, including its minor 240Pu/241Am contributions, not a separately isolated pure-239Pu decay rate.

The idealized epsilon_0(0,0) is the monitor counting efficiency for an infinitesimally narrow beam striking the deposit center at the 2200 m/s reference speed. Conversion from the monochromatic response uses lambda_0/lambda_mono under the inverse-velocity assumption. Finite beam profile, target absorption and self-shielding corrections separate this quantity from an uncorrected measured count ratio. Both alpha and triton capture products contribute; this is not a neutron survival probability.

The thesis and detailed article describe the calibration associated with the earlier beam-lifetime monitor, not new neutron-lifetime acquisitions. The thesis Table 7.1 lists 27 runs from June-December 2010; the 2018 text repeats that range, while Figure 22 includes a March 2011 point. The exact mapping of runs, ancillary measurements and revised analysis across the 2011 thesis, 2013 lifetime update and 2018 article remains unresolved.

The thesis uses two spacer configurations and the Cu-Cu-1 aperture, diameter 25.6725+/-0.0030 mm. The 2018 article reports a nickel-coated copper aperture of 25.765192+/-0.000240 mm and source distance 87.4226+/-0.0015 mm, with different alpha rates and activity. Their reported source calibrations cannot be substituted or averaged as independent determinations of an identically specified preparation. No cross-version correction or physical source-aging estimate is established.

The 2018 article reports the corrected alpha count rate 125.740 per second and effective Omega_stack=0.0053415, followed by R_Pu=23538.4 per second. Their printed central quotient is 23540.204... per second, and display-rounding intervals do not include the reported activity center. Additional input or correction reconciliation is unresolved. This is a failure to reconstruct the printed result from those displayed inputs, not evidence that the experimental numerical analysis is wrong.

The beam analysis uses timed beam-on minus beam-off rates, the geometric mean of top and bottom gamma-detector rates, and thin-target/thick-target/thin-target cycles to suppress first-order gamma-efficiency drift. Gamma backgrounds, thresholds, pulse pileup, dead time and silicon-capture contributions remain explicit corrections; a count-rate ratio is not a raw absolute neutron count.

Within-campaign gamma-detector drift controls are distinct from the long-term 6Li-deposit and aperture stability assumptions needed to transfer a later calibration to the 2000-2001 lifetime acquisition. The thesis Chapter 8 treated that transfer as unresolved; the separately reviewed 2013 update adopts its stated temporal-stability model. No deposit-loss posterior or historical transfer is independently reproduced here.

Cancellation of nuclear normalization inputs in the ideal rate identity does not eliminate nuclear data from every correction. The detailed article uses neutron scattering/absorption inputs, radiative-capture cross sections, material attenuation and modeled neutron/gamma transport. Its remaining upstream nuclear data, image records and simulation implementations are not independently reproduced.

The wavelength is inferred from silicon Bragg measurements on the same beam, including a lambda/2 component correction. Unexplained angle excursions are retained and the wavelength uncertainty uses a conservative observed spread, rather than only the uncertainty of the weighted centroid. The wavelength fit and transport simulations are not replayed.

The 27 reported calibration points span three collimations and two gamma detectors with common and configuration-specific corrections. The article describes Gaussian variation of correction inputs followed by weighted constant fits. These points, detector channels and publications do not supply independent replications of the calibration standard; full correction covariance, exact grouping and analysis code are not recovered from printed tables.

Equation 28 in the 2018 article omits the factor 1/2 required to invert Equation 12, which counts both alpha and triton products. Equation 26 defines phi_abs as an absorbed fraction near 0.01016, but the later text labels the transmission correction 0.989846 as phi_abs. These printed formula/notation conflicts are retained; no claim is made that the numerical implementation followed them.

The thesis reports epsilon_0^AG=(3.1116+/-0.0016)e-5, the 2013 lifetime paper uses (3.1098+/-0.0017)e-5, and the detailed 2018 article reports idealized epsilon_0(0,0)=(3.1101+/-0.0018)e-5. Source-specific normalization, metrology, corrections and aggregation must be reconciled before substitution. No new lifetime is calculated from the 2018 value and these reports are not averaged.

Alpha-source activity, monitor count efficiency and a neutron-decay lifetime are different quantities. None establishes nucleon formation, eternal proton stability, a universal constituent minimum or a unique explanation of beam/bottle differences.

limitations: Baryon number and net flavor are additive sector labels in the stated strong-interaction description. They do not specify a total quark, antiquark or gluon population, sector probabilities, a free-particle census or weak-decay stability.

The three-factor minimum concerns nonempty tensor powers of the fundamental color representation without antiquarks or adjoint factors. It is not a minimum for arbitrary color representations, every hadron, or a graph construction rule. Color SU(3) and approximate flavor SU(3) are distinct.

The Fock expansion is a representation with specified quantization, gauge, regulator and renormalization conventions. No coefficient, Hamiltonian eigenstate, parton distribution, mass, magnetic response or formation trajectory is computed here.
The executable establishes exact algebra under declared definitions. It neither proves confinement nor shows that a color-invariant tensor is a dynamically realized or stable physical particle.
claims.scope: Declared QCD occupation-basis labels, additive flavor charges and fundamental color representations; no empirical constituent census or bound-state solution.
claims.statement: In the declared strong-interaction nucleon sectors, net flavor means quarks minus antiquarks: proton (N_u,N_d)=(2,1), neutron (1,2), with zero other net flavors. With B=sum_f N_f/3 and Q/e=sum_f q_f*N_f, these labels give B=1 and charges +1 and 0. Adding a same-flavor quark-antiquark pair or gluons preserves these additive labels without preserving total basis-particle count.

limitations: The channel is an isolated ground-state bare deuteron with no supplied energy and asymptotically free p+p+e-+electron-antineutrino final particles. Its net charge is +1 on both sides. Neutral atoms, electronic bound final states, molecular ions and externally driven breakup are different state specifications.

Q0 neglects the antineutrino rest mass; any nonnegative final neutrino mass raises the required rest energy. Positive-energy on-shell final particles and four-momentum conservation make Q0<0 an exclusion for this channel. Q0>=0 alone would not establish a nonzero matrix element or rate.

The calculation uses the one Rau joint adjusted pair mp=1.007276466580(17)u and md=2.013553212537(16)u with correlation +0.26. These reuse the published mass measurements and molecular/reference inputs; the local adjustment, direct deuteron and earlier proton values are not substituted or pooled as independent replicas.

The adopted CODATA 2018 inputs are me=0.000548579909065(16)u and u*c^2=931494102.42(28)eV. They are external adjustment values, not new electron-mass or energy-conversion measurements; this calculation does not update them to a later adjustment.

The admitted neutron mass was inferred as mn=md-mp+Bd/c^2 using the same adjusted masses and capture binding. Substitution into (mn-mp-me)c^2-Bd cancels Bd identically. Capture-derived mn and Bd are not independent confirmation of the reduced Q and cannot be assigned independent errors in that expression.

Separately inserting printed mn=1.00866491604u and Bd/c^2=0.00238817008u gives a Q larger by 0.0027944823...eV than the reduced expression. The identity gives mn=1.008664916037u, compatible with the printed neutron rounding; the difference is not a source-analysis error or a second acquisition. The display-rounding box is not a confidence interval.

The published +0.26 mass-pair correlation enters var(md-2mp)=var(md)+4var(mp)-4cov(md,mp), giving about 0.0313eV standard uncertainty for this contribution alone. Electron/reference cross-covariances and the full adjustment are not reconstructed; no complete Q uncertainty, discovery significance or calibrated coverage is supplied.

Bare nuclear masses cannot be replaced by neutral hydrogen-isotope masses. For positive electronic binding energies IH and ID, Q0=[M(D)-2M(H)]c^2+ID-2IH. This identity retains the declared bare-particle channel; it does not import a neutral-atom decay or its final electronic states.

This is a new bounded calculation from published inputs, not a beta-decay measurement reported by Rau. It establishes neither all-channel deuteron permanence, a nuclear or individual bound-neutron lifetime, nor stability of arbitrary nuclei. No weak amplitude, phase-space rate, raw mass fit, instrument calibration or complete covariance is reproduced.

limitations: The u,d,s q-qbar model supplies flavor labels and multiplets, not a complete hadronic Fock state, exact constituent census, physical formation sequence or color-SU(3) result. Only the lightest pseudoscalar/vector assignments are retained; scalar/excited/exotic assignments and universal parent weights/minima are excluded.

Physical isoscalars with the same quantum numbers mix. The two-state basis rotation does not make eta and eta-prime exact pure octet/singlet states or establish their full state content. A single flavor-basis pseudoscalar angle assumes the stated treatment of OZI-violating terms; generic beyond-leading-order descriptions need not use one angle.

The reported 41.4-degree result assumes zero eta-prime gluonium and Equation 10, including constituent mass ratio m_s/m_bar, C_NS/C_S overlap parameters, vector mixing phi_V=3.4 degrees and the photon-momentum ratio cubed. These are model/external inputs, not determined by R_phi alone. The theoretical error is a maximum variation over the adopted parameter spreads, not a locally derived Gaussian uncertainty.
claims.scope: Selected light-flavor meson classification and KLOE 2001-2002 radiative ratio with conditional mixing; no universal formation claim.
claims.statement: The flavor-octet and singlet isoscalar basis vectors are (|u ubar>+|d dbar>-2|s sbar>)/sqrt(6) and (|u ubar>+|d dbar>+|s sbar>)/sqrt(3). Physical eta and eta-prime are rotated combinations, not exact octet/singlet labels. In the restricted flavor basis |eta>=cos(phi_P)*|q qbar>-sin(phi_P)*|s sbar> and |eta-prime>=sin(phi_P)*|q qbar>+cos(phi_P)*|s sbar>, with |q qbar>=(|u ubar>+|d dbar>)/sqrt(2) and theta_P=phi_P-arctan(sqrt(2)). Each ket labels a quark-antiquark basis state, not a subtraction or a complete observed particle population.

limitations: The reported fit uses 70 particle-type, momentum and zenith bins, weighted Monte Carlo statistics and nuisance penalties from Equations 2-4 and Table II. Overall normalization alpha floats freely despite an estimated 25% prior uncertainty; it is not included as a 25% Gaussian constraint. The v2 multi-GeV FC mu-like weight contains (1-rho*N_PC/(2*N_mu)), whereas PC has (1+rho/2). Neither weights, response, minimization, contour coverage nor significance are locally reconstructed.

The physical best fit has sin^2(2 theta)=1 and Delta m^2=2.2e-3 eV^2; the unconstrained minimum at sin^2(2 theta)=1.05 lies outside the physical region. Reported confidence contours are referenced to the physical minimum with the authors' bounded-region prescription, not generic two-parameter thresholds supplied locally. This is a historical effective two-flavor mass-squared difference, not an absolute mass, a modern three-flavor global fit or a mass-generation mechanism.

The nu_mu-to-nu_tau simulation neglects tau appearance and decay because of the small expected yield. The source explicitly says this sample cannot distinguish nu_mu-to-nu_tau from disappearance into a non-interacting sterile species; it does not directly observe tau appearance. Its separate nu_mu-to-nu_e comparison includes Earth matter effects and is disfavored within the tested model, not an exclusion of every alternative theory.

citations.locator: 2025 review pages 10-12, Section 14.5 and Equations 14.49-14.58: coherent forward potentials, neutral matter, propagation basis and particle-sign conventions
citations.note: Supports the selected formal convention and its stated model limits; no experimental inference is admitted by this definition.

limitations: Use a closed unitary three-active-neutrino model with standard weak interactions, hbar=c=1 and fixed positive energy in the ultrarelativistic coherent forward-scattering approximation. The prescribed medium is electrically neutral, unpolarized and locally isotropic, with nonrelativistic electrons, protons and neutrons and no appreciable muon/tau population. Incoherent scattering, absorption, neutrino-neutrino refraction, sterile states and nonstandard interactions require different models.

The vector f contains flavor amplitudes, with the already declared U_alpha,i convention. The review writes its basic evolution equation in the vacuum mass basis; multiplication by the constant U gives the stated flavor-basis Hamiltonian. For antineutrinos both U becomes U* and the charged-current potential changes sign. A merely diagonal potential cannot in general be discarded; the neutral-current term is removable here because it is common to all three active flavors.

Vacuum masses, the mixing matrix, energy and the medium density profile are supplied inputs. Matter-dependent eigenvalues are effective propagation parameters, not newly generated vacuum masses. This model does not determine absolute mass, Dirac/Majorana nature, an origin mechanism, universal carrier minima or a temporal emergence order.

A variable density generally gives noncommuting Hamiltonians at different positions. Its evolution requires the ordered solution with initial conditions; one cannot substitute a single constant-density vacuum phase or assume adiabaticity from an instantaneous mixing angle. No actual solar/Earth profile, scattering experiment, oscillation fit or matter evolution is numerically reproduced here.
claims.scope: Formal coherent propagation in a prescribed ordinary medium and its stated two-flavor approximation; no empirical mass-generation or solar-fit claim.
claims.statement: For flavor amplitudes f, i*df/dx=H_f(x)*f with H_f=U diag(m_i^2) U-dagger/(2E)+diag(V_e(x),0,0), after removing a common identity term. For neutrinos V_e=sqrt(2)*G_F*n_e(x); for antineutrinos U is complex-conjugated and V_e changes sign. For neutrinos in neutral ordinary matter the active-sector neutral-current contribution is -G_F*n_n(x)/sqrt(2) times the identity and changes only a common phase; its sign also reverses for antineutrinos before removal.

It is not an exact reduction of every three-flavor preparation. The sine and cosine specify the angle branch; tan(2 theta_m) alone is insufficient.

A=Delta*cos(2 theta) gives maximal instantaneous mixing only when the off-diagonal mixing and gap are nonzero. Resonance by itself does not establish adiabatic following, complete flavor conversion, equal observed event rates or an experimentally selected mechanism. If f=R(x)*a in an instantaneous eigenbasis, i*da/dx=[diag(lambda_i)-i*R-dagger*dR/dx]*a. Abrupt changes or a small gap can invalidate that approximation. No solar survival probability or fitted density profile is supplied.

A variable density generally gives noncommuting Hamiltonians at different positions. Its evolution requires the ordered solution with initial conditions; one cannot substitute a single constant-density vacuum phase or assume adiabaticity from an instantaneous mixing angle. No actual solar/Earth profile, scattering experiment, oscillation fit or matter evolution is numerically reproduced here.

Vacuum masses, the mixing matrix, energy and the medium density profile are supplied inputs. Matter-dependent eigenvalues are effective propagation parameters, not newly generated vacuum masses. claims.statement: In the declared two-flavor approximation set A=2E*(V_e-V_x) and Delta_m=sqrt[(Delta*cos(2 theta)-A)^2+(Delta*sin(2 theta))^2]. An instantaneous eigenbasis has the additional connection -i*R-dagger*dR/dx; adiabatic following is an approximation that neglects its inter-state coupling relative to the gap.
