studies.finding: The Bax manipulation increases surviving cell labels and selected LTP and behavioral responses. It supports task-specific intervention effects, while unique mediation by neuron number and irradiation-based cognitive necessity remain unresolved.
limitations: NCff mice carry Nestin-CreERT2 and two floxed Bax alleles on a mixed C57BL/6-129/SvEv background. The primary contrast is tamoxifen versus vehicle within NCff, starting at at least eight weeks. Reporter NCY versus NCffY comparisons use separate littermate groups both receiving tamoxifen; Cre-negative Bax-floxed controls are another comparison.

The manipulation reduces Bax-dependent cell death in the Nestin stem/progenitor lineage; it is not a selective increase in birth rate or a dentate-newborn-neuron-only intervention. Olfactory-bulb survival also changes. Reporter recombination is a proxy, and altered cell properties or other lineage effects remain alternative mediators.

Behavioral testing is generally at 14-18 weeks with both sexes, but fear conditioning, discrimination, extinction and clearance use males. Experiments and analyses were blinded to genotype or treatment. A complete randomized allocation, exclusion, cage and prospective sample-size manifest is not reported.

The eight-week dentate BrdU assay labels on days 9-18 and counts on day 56; only a subset is NeuN-positive. Counts, marker fractions, proliferation and mature output are distinct. The olfactory and running BrdU schedules differ. Reporter neuron counts per section are not whole-dentate totals.

Weak-tetanus LTP is a population field response, not a birthdated single-cell recording. Eight-week assays without bicuculline use eight slices/six vehicle mice and eleven slices/seven tamoxifen mice; with bicuculline they use four slices/three vehicle and six slices/three tamoxifen mice. Slice-level statistics do not reconstruct animal-level independence.

Main Figure 2c alternates the order of contexts across days, whereas the discrimination Methods describe training context A followed one hour later by similar context B. The exact per-animal schedule requires reconciliation. The nine-day ratio analysis reports treatment P=0.023; its day F/degree-of-freedom/P combination also needs correction. Handling of a zero sum of freezing scores is unspecified.

Contextual freezing discrimination is a behavioral proxy for pattern separation, not a direct measurement of DG neural population codes or general memory improvement. Supplementary protocol variants have treatment P=0.38 and P=0.06 despite interactions or day-specific differences; they cannot be pooled as uniformly positive main effects.

Irradiation uses separate ten-week-old Bax-floxed mice and three 5 Gy exposures on days 1, 4 and 8, with behavior four months later. Regional irradiation is not a selective newborn-neuron ablation or a rescue experiment. Recall samples are eight sham/nine irradiated mice, versus seven/nine in discrimination; the missing sham inclusion is unresolved.

Supplementary Figure 14 reports an overall discrimination-ratio treatment P=0.1 and interaction P=0.3. Late within-group differences are not a between-group necessity test. Its day-five F(1,14)=4.34/P=0.04 pair needs reconciliation; no replacement biological P value is calculated here.

Running is a shared-cage exposure: two wheels for four to five mice, beginning five weeks after treatment. Figure 4 shows behavior on days 64-84. Individual running dose and cage independence are unresolved. Increased locomotion complicates an isolated anxiety interpretation, and home-cage activity has a separate sample.

Reported null outcomes are assay- and cohort-specific, not equivalence tests. Supplementary Figure 18 contains invalid negative F notation and conflicting novelty-suppressed-feeding significance; Figure 19 has a control-label conflict. Figure 20 contains a malformed marker percentage. These values are not silently corrected or admitted as quantitative defaults.

Granule-layer volume Methods and caption disagree on group size. Sholl analysis selects complex neurons and traces collapsed z-stacks; its null is not a unique three-dimensional geometry. Axon-length and cell-count cohorts cannot establish packing density or a complete output route without matched measurements.

Main experimental text and Methods, all four main figures, and the text of all 28 supplement pages were read. Supplementary pages 5, 16-19, 24 and 26-27 were visually inspected. Raw recordings, animal-level behavioral data and executable analysis code were not obtained or replayed.

Null object-recognition, water-maze, avoidance, extinction and clearance endpoints do not mean that every measured behavior is unchanged: the novel-object habituation locomotor interaction is significant. Multiple cohorts and distinct pre- and post-training manipulation schedules must remain separate.

studies.finding: Novel motor training is accompanied by increased formation and elimination in selected cortical dendrites, and initially new spines are preferentially retained. The results constrain experience-dependent remodeling without proving a unique memory substrate or a universal construction law.
limitations: YFP-H mice were one month old or older than four months. Superficial apical dendrites of layer V pyramidal neurons were imaged 10-100 micrometers below the cortical surface under ketamine-xylazine anesthesia; these are selected cortical compartments, not a whole-brain connectome.

Main scientific text, Methods Summary and Figures 1-4 are reviewed. All text of the 12-page publisher supplement, Figures S1-S5 and Table S1 are reviewed, including visual inspection. The separate full Methods file and movie were not obtained or read; precise task procedures, sex, allocation, blinding and exclusions remain unverified.

Dense labeling prevented tracing complete individual neurons. The supplementary estimate of 20-80 sampled cells per mouse is not an identified neuron census. The study total of 32079 spines in 209 mice does not make spines independent animals or mean that every spine was followed for 120 days.

Formation and elimination are interval-specific percentages relative to the initial spine count. New-spine survival uses the newly appearing subset instead. These denominators cannot be exchanged or converted into universal growth rates, absolute density or graph weights.

General controls were littermates with the same food restriction and similar handling, without shaping or training. Learning, task exposure and reward are not individually isolated. Animal-level image stacks, cohort assignments and analysis code were not obtained; published tests were not independently reproduced.

The Figure 1f first-session training group selected four mice with more than ten successes in thirty reaches. Figure 1g also plots animals with ten or fewer successes, so the correlation cohort is not this selected four-mouse group. Imaging occurred within one hour after the session, but the baseline was from the previous day; this interval does not timestamp each spine birth within an hour.

Behavioral curves, spine-turnover cohorts and follow-up cohorts have different animal counts. The survival design uses two classification images and a third follow-up at a selected interval; it is not one fully sampled trajectory through every plotted timepoint.

Figure 2c normalizes total spine number to the initial image. Both control and trained trajectories lie below their initial value by day 16. Convergence toward control levels is distinct from the abstract wording about return to the original level; no exact count setpoint or one-for-one replacement is demonstrated.

Spine morphology does not directly measure synaptic currents, presynaptic partner identity or memory content. The study does not selectively remove the retained spines to test memory necessity or uniquely assign different memories to disjoint synaptic sets.

Motor mapping was terminal in fourteen mice: five imaging regions lay within the forelimb map, six on its border and three outside but within 300 micrometers. The map was not followed longitudinally, and distance from its border does not identify a complete circuit or a construction geometry.

Named nonsignificant comparisons are not equivalence tests. The long-duration activity controls had marked attrition: only two mice still reached more than twenty times daily at day eight and one at day sixteen. They do not support a well-powered universal exclusion of motor activity.

Spine-size analysis used head diameter divided by adjacent shaft diameter in 29 surviving spines; the cited supplementary paragraph does not supply its animal count. This selected morphological ratio is neither absolute spine volume nor measured synaptic strength.

Persistence to the reported approximately 120-day follow-up is finite. Training for sixteen days followed by the long untrained interval does not demonstrate permanence, a globally minimal circuit or a unique homeostatic construction law.

studies.finding: Selected peri-infarct samples show increased spine formation and altered morphology after photothrombosis. Recovery cohorts, optical readouts and spatial comparisons constrain injury-associated remodeling without proving behavioral restoration or a unique construction mechanism.
limitations: Adult male C57BL6 YFP-H mice were approximately 2.5-7 months old. Layer 5 neuronal apical tufts were sampled within the superficial 100 micrometers, typically 100-500 micrometers from the posterior-medial infarct edge; this is selected surviving cortex, not the whole injured brain.

Main scientific text, Materials and Methods, and Figures 1-5 with captions are reviewed. Supplemental Figures 1-2 were not obtained or read. Animal-identified image stacks, custom IgorPro routines and the allocation/exclusion manifest were not obtained; no imaging or biological experiment was independently reproduced.

Photothrombosis used Rose Bengal 100 milligrams per kilogram intraperitoneally and 532-nanometer illumination, 17 milliwatts for fifteen minutes, under ketamine-xylazine. Sham controls omitted either dye or illumination. Per-assay sham composition, random allocation and group-specific age distributions are not supplied in the reviewed account.

Imaging under urethane was acute: hourly stacks over six, occasionally seven hours, after a one-, two- or six-week recovery interval, followed by terminal histology. Separate cohorts do not trace the same spine or dendritic arbor continuously from before injury through six weeks.

Only laterally projecting spines were scored. New spines had to protrude at least four pixels, approximately 0.55 micrometers, and remain present at the six-hour endpoint. Transient events, filopodium conversions, shifted segments and poor-quality images were excluded. The assay is not a census of all spine births, losses or synapses.

Turnover is reported as a percentage of the counted spine population over the imaging session; raw animal-level numerator/denominator assignments are unavailable. Spine density is a count per ten micrometers of dendrite. Neither measure is a neuron birth rate, a universal hourly turnover constant or a calibrated graph weight.

Turnover scoring was blinded to experimental condition, but movement, abnormal breathing and image deterioration could exclude experiments; exclusion counts and animal identifiers are not supplied. Axial optical resolution was about 5.3 micrometers, much poorer than lateral resolution, and six spine-appearance cases were pooled across animals for shaft-fluorescence controls.

Spine morphology and adjacent sensory-evoked reflectance do not measure the functional efficacy of each new synapse, selective memory content or behavioral recovery. The Discussion explicitly leaves the causal link between increased formation and recovered function unestablished.

The main text gives a 0.14 percent control formation mean and 1.37, 0.93 and 0.75 percent poststroke means. The abstract describes a five- to eight-fold peak increase; these rounded quantities do not define one exact fold estimate. Retain the reported assay means without calibrating a universal multiplier.

The six-week density cohort reports five mice versus six controls but t(8)=1.43, P=0.09. The three-mouse near/far comparison reports t(3)=4.87, P<0.01 for formation and t(3)=1.92, P=0.08 for elimination. Sidedness and statistical units need resolution before numerical reproduction; these degrees of freedom do not establish an ordinary paired three-mouse test.

Orientation uses projected 15-30 micrometer segments, eighteen ten-degree bins, and three mice per group, with the infarct placed at a common reference position. Reported F(17,17) tests concern bin-distribution variance; bins are not independent mice and this is not an animal-level circular-statistical reconstruction.

The authors consider mechanical distortion during tissue loss and scar formation as well as growth and retraction. Projected dendrite-vessel alignment does not isolate shared guidance, establish physical contact or prove an optimal generative network geometry.

Texas Red dextran labels plasma. Capillary velocity in micrometers per second is distinct from volumetric perfusion; fluorescent vessel volume fraction is distinct from vessel number, connectivity and selectively demonstrated angiogenesis. The vascular cohort totals fourteen animals but per-timepoint assignments and segmentation routines remain unresolved.

The near/far spine comparison uses approximately 0.33 versus 1.65 millimeters from the infarct edge at two weeks. This is different from the orientation comparison of less than 250 versus 500-800 micrometers at six weeks. Restricted ipsilateral sampling does not establish absence of remodeling elsewhere.

Nonsignificant outcomes are not equivalence or full recovery. Photothrombosis does not permit controlled reperfusion, and the paper does not directly establish the same time course in other stroke models, traumatic injury or humans.

studies.finding: Dentate BrdU-positive cells include cells with neuronal markers. The clinical sampling, labeling assumptions and lack of functional assays limit birth-rate, lifespan and circuit-integration conclusions.
limitations: Five cancer patients received diagnostic BrdU labeling; one patient with similar cancer and no BrdU served as a staining control. This is an observational autopsy series, not a randomized intervention on neurogenesis or a healthy-population survey.

Figure 2 pairs ages at death of 72, 58, 57, 68 and 67 years with 16, 136, 274, 393 and 781 days after infusion. Different people supply the intervals; their bars are not longitudinal survival measurements of one cohort or an age-controlled birth-rate curve.

A single intravenous infusion contained 250 mg BrdU in 100 ml saline. No anticancer therapy was given before or during labeling and no cerebral metastases were found at autopsy. Later treatment, full clinical histories, sex-specific sampling, postmortem intervals and selection or exclusion counts are not reconstructable from the report.

BrdU marks DNA synthesis and subsequent label retention. The neuronal-marker interpretation supports candidate adult-born cells under the labeling assumptions; the images do not continuously observe cell division, trace a clone or selectively exclude every nonmitotic DNA-synthesis mechanism.

NeuN, NSE and calbindin were alternative neuronal stains with BrdU and GFAP, not three independent birthdating assays or necessarily three labels on each same cell. Reported neuronal percentages use BrdU-positive cells as denominator, not all neurons. At least twenty BrdU-positive cells per patient were examined; exact marker-specific denominators and patient-level counts are unavailable.

BrdU/GFAP-positive cells and cells lacking the selected phenotype markers were also observed. Marker-negative cells cannot be assigned automatically to a quiescent stem-cell lineage, and fractions from different marker assays cannot be added as disjoint cell classes.

Figure 2 densities use five to seven sections per person and cells per cubic millimeter of sampled tissue. Error bars summarize section sampling within a person, not additional independent patients. Densities are not whole-hippocampus totals or daily neuron production.

The optical-disector calculation uses the 40-micrometer microtome setting; actual processed thickness and shrinkage were not reconstructed. Sections are at least 240 micrometers apart. The defined SGZ extends one cell diameter into the granule layer and two below it, so compartment totals must not be obtained by simply adding GCL and SGZ densities.

The uninfused control tests labeling background; failure to detect BrdU in that person does not demonstrate absence of neurogenesis. Untreated-section, wavelength, confocal z-series and brightfield controls constrain staining artifacts without independently validating every retained cell.

SVZ BrdU-positive cells lacked detectable NeuN and GFAP in the reported assay, whose double-label data are not shown. This does not demonstrate neuronal differentiation, directed migration, or absence of SVZ progenitors. Figure 1e caption mixes human and rat descriptions; panel-specific species identity remains unresolved.

The paper explicitly leaves functional significance untested. No electrical recording, identified synaptic output, behavioral mediation or selective birth-cell perturbation establishes functional integration in these human samples. Findings in mouse integration experiments cannot supply those missing human measurements.

Raw sections, image stacks, individual counts and analysis code have not been reproduced. The small clinical series does not establish an invariant rate, every adult age or a universal structural-construction rule.

studies.finding: The isotope profiles support postnatal DNA synthesis under the birthdating assumptions. Renewal fractions, rates and survival schedules depend on the selected scenario, sample inclusion and external anatomical counts; functional integration and population feedback were not measured.
limitations: The accepted supplement starts with 156 fractions (74 NeuN-positive and 82 NeuN-negative), retains 55 and 65 for isotope analysis, and uses 51 and 64 for individual 2POP fits after four neuronal and one nonneuronal exclusions. Paired analyses use 40 pairs. These are different analysis populations, not 120 independent donors.

This is an observational autopsy study, not a randomized neurogenesis intervention. Main text gives ages 19-92, but accepted Table S1 includes NeuN-negative pub_id 53 aged 16.2. Table S1 also contains pre-2000 death dates despite the stated 2000-2012 tissue procurement interval. Donor identity, procurement chronology, clinical selection, exclusions and the final sample manifest need reconciliation.

Accepted Table S1 gives different birth-date/age entries for the two fractions labeled pub_id 49, while neuronal pub_id 69 and nonneuronal pub_id 68 share displayed age, birth/death dates and sex. Neither identical metadata nor matching pub_id alone establishes the complete paired donor manifest.

AMS measures bulk genomic-DNA carbon-14, reported as fraction modern or decay-corrected delta carbon-14. These are isotope concentrations, not counts of new neurons or single-cell birth timestamps. The method integrates DNA synthesis under assumptions about atmospheric carbon and the food chain.

NeuN sorting separates marker-positive nuclei from a heterogeneous marker-negative fraction, which includes several glial and vascular-associated cell types. Representative Figure S1 purities are not the purity of every sample; Table S1 includes neuronal sorting purity of 79%. Linear mixture correction does not independently validate cell lineage, and nonneuronal NA fields are not zero contamination.

AMS was blinded to sample age and origin. This does not establish blinding of all collection, selection or modeling. The main instrumental error description does not replace the sample-specific SD columns. Accepted Table S1 includes unresolved SD entries, such as F14C SD 1.01 alongside delta carbon-14 SD 14.00 for neuronal pub_id 21; values have not been silently corrected.

The birthdating interpretation assumes stable DNA after the last division and new cells arising from an actively proliferating progenitor pool. DNA synthesis is not a continuously observed division or clone. An old postmitotic reservoir migrating into the tissue was not modeled; the discussion of DNA repair includes unpublished stroke observations and does not selectively test every alternative.

Whole hippocampi were analyzed; the investigators could not separately radiocarbon-date hippocampal subdivisions. Dentate localization and absolute cell-number scaling rely on other histological and stereological studies. The approximately 700 neurons per day in each hippocampus and 0.004% of dentate neurons per day are model-dependent estimates, not directly counted daily births.

Global neuronal 2POP fitting reports a renewing fraction near 0.35, with a reported 95% interval of 0.12-0.63. For nonneuronal cells the main text reports 0.51 with interval 0.22-0.88, accepted Table S2 gives 0.56, and individual fits fix 0.55. These summaries must not be treated as one exactly reproduced estimate.

The reported individual medians, 1.75% per year for neurons and 3.5% for nonneuronal cells, apply within fixed renewing fractions of 0.35 and 0.55 after the stated exclusions. Global-fit rates of about 12% and 4.9% per year in Tables S3 and S2 are different estimands. Unfittable samples were excluded from the individual 2POP analysis; Figure 2C/5A additionally states plot limits below 0.001 or above 1.5.

The accepted supplement distinguishes unpaired 2POP comparison (51 neuronal and 64 nonneuronal fractions, rank-sum P=0.005) from 40 matched pairs (signed-rank P=0.054; neuronal median 1.5%, nonneuronal 3.5% per year). The latter null does not establish equal rates. Comparing these tests without their populations and denominators would be misleading.

Age associations use cross-sectional, model-derived rates: reported neuronal r=-0.31, P=0.03 and nonneuronal r=-0.35, P=0.04. They do not trace the same people over time or identify an age intervention. The sex comparison P=0.41 does not establish equivalence. The DCX overlay uses an external Knoth cohort, not birthdating of the same cells.

The accepted supplement prints a heuristic labeled AIC, p + log2(SSE), and requires a halving of SSE per added parameter. Applying that printed rule to rounded Table S2 gives 0.31 > 0.51/2, so its nonneuronal 2POP preference does not follow from that rule. Table S3 has 0.17 < 0.49/2 for neurons. This arithmetic checks reporting consistency only; final supplementary methods, likelihood and code remain unverified.

The source says subjects born around 1955-1965 discriminate 2POP from homogeneous age-dependent alternatives; without them the scenarios could not be distinguished. MCMC explores bounded parameter sets, and fitting several scenarios does not prove a unique biological mechanism. Full numerical replay and out-of-sample discrimination have not been performed.

The fitting procedure assumes a one-year food lag and development beginning six months before birth. Its weighted SSE squares weights of 1 or 2 assigned around a 10-microgram carbon boundary. Table S1 has both estimated DNA carbon mass and reactor-measured mass, including ND entries. The exact mass choice, boundary treatment and missing-value policy require executable code before reproducing the fit.

Figure 6 illustrates 2POPEd with initial renewing fraction 0.31, nonrenewing death rate 0.0035 per year, newborn death rate 0.11 per year and death-rate half-reduction age 19 years. The chosen set belongs to the best 3% of 300,000 explored sets; it is not a uniquely identified law. The reported 7.1-year half-life and external stereological age profiles are model-linked summaries, not longitudinal tracking of those human neurons.

The supplement explicitly does not explore population feedback: birth and death rates do not depend on the population state. Constant population size in replacement scenarios is imposed by their birth boundary, not observed emergence of a stabilizing rule. Population turnover does not identify one-for-one functional replacement, circuit topology or a universal minimal assembly.

No human electrical, identified synaptic-output or selective behavioral assay is performed. Similar estimated rates across species do not supply human functional integration or a birth-to-cognition mechanism. Histology, isotope dating, molecular markers and rodent interventions remain distinct evidence.

studies.finding: The reported marker combinations support adult macaque dentate neuronal and oligodendroglial production under the labeling assumptions. They do not identify a universal rate, common multipotent founder, observed migration, replacement feedback or cognitive function.
studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
limitations: Ten adult macaques of both sexes include Macaca mulatta and Macaca fascicularis, aged 5.5-16.5 years. The paper does not provide an animal-by-species, sex, age, dosing, survival and assay manifest. Ten injected animals do not establish ten independent animals for every neuronal or glial endpoint.

Intravenous BrdU was 50 mg/kg, either once or daily for five consecutive days, administered between 09:00 and noon. Materials and Methods lists survival times ending at 72 days, whereas Results twice gives 75 days as the maximum. The reference injection for that discrepancy is not reconciled; neither value is silently selected.

BrdU and PCNA label DNA synthesis or cell-cycle-associated profiles; they do not continuously observe completed cytokinesis or a clone. PCNA was examined in sections from the same brains, not as a second independent animal cohort or a reported same-cell BrdU/PCNA lineage assay. Apposed doublets suggest, but do not identify, sibling relationships.

Early and later regional labeling is compared across sacrificed animals. BrdU-positive cells at the longest interval are not specifically identified as neurons. Label retention does not establish the survival fraction of a birth cohort, a neuron-specific lifespan, absence of rapid turnover elsewhere or absence of BrdU toxicity.

Neuronal double labeling was examined 32 days after the last of five injections in PFA-fixed 40-micrometre cryosections. Twenty nonadjacent sections were examined for each of NeuN and TuJ1; these are section counts, not independent animals. Exact biological replication, section sampling, denominators and uncertainty are not supplied for the reported averages.

BrdU/NeuN and BrdU/TuJ1 are alternative marker assays, not a reported three-marker identity for every labeled cell. The study reports neuronal colabels in GCL/SGZ and none in the other examined hippocampal regions; sampling and marker sensitivity do not establish absolute regional absence. Raw confocal stacks, optical section positions and segmentation have not been reanalysed.

Fluorophore reversal, omitted-primary controls and Figure 2c-d address staining and channel artifacts. They do not establish lineage, complete specificity or quantified sensitivity. Antibody omission is not a biological no-neurogenesis control, and no matched dose-control experiment establishes BrdU safety.

O4 or CNP double labeling used sequential black nuclear and brown cytoplasmic peroxidase signals in ethanol-fixed paraffin sections of 8 or 10 micrometres. Figure 3 shows 27-day single-injection examples. These preparations are distinct from the 32-day neuronal fluorescence assay; marker-positive morphology does not measure myelin formation or conduction.

Astrocyte generation is attributed to Eckenhoff and Rakic (1988) and Eriksson et al. (1998), not a newly reported GFAP assay in this experiment. Finding several phenotypes near one niche does not establish a shared multipotent founder, self-renewal or exclusive stem-cell lineage. The 1988 GFAP/autoradiographic assays are separately reviewed and do not trace a common founder.

The approximately 1,000 BrdU/TuJ1-positive cells per hippocampus is extrapolated from about two profiles per section, 40-micrometre sections and an approximately 19-mm external anatomical length. Scaling by an external 4.8-million-neuron estimate and dividing by five injections gives the provisional 0.004% per day. This is not a direct daily birth count or an unbiased whole-hippocampus stereological census.

Five-day cumulative labeling followed by 32 days of survival combines labeling opportunity, subsequent division, dilution, survival and marker expression. A single retained-label estimate does not identify production and death separately. The paper itself leaves lower production versus lower survival unresolved. No empirical edge weight or universal rate is assigned.

The roughly tenfold rodent comparison uses a separate published mouse study and external denominators. The paper acknowledges unmatched age, species, environment, labeling and survival procedures. Absolute-age and relative-age hypotheses were not compared in one matched design, and this series supplies no invariant primate-to-human scaling.

Bipolar morphology and radial or tangential orientation support a migration interpretation but do not track displacement, origin or a radial-glial guidance interaction. Nearby cells are not a clone, and anatomical resemblance to developing neurons is not an executed construction rule.

The replacement interpretation draws on separate human neuron counts and macaque synapse counts. Synapse-count stability is not a matched neuron census. This experiment measures neither paired births and deaths, feedback of population state, replacement identity nor the fraction of older neurons ultimately renewed.

No electrical, synaptic-output, learning or memory assay was performed. A possible cognitive role, stable-memory benefit or recovery mechanism remains untested. Labeling in this study does not require an injury or learning manipulation and does not validate the source card's necessary incoming assertions, weights or minimum carrier counts.

studies.finding: Young and middle-aged macaques show neuronal colabels after longer labeling intervals. Aged S-phase profiles, marker age differences, migration and hormonal explanations require separate interpretation.
studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
limitations: Eleven animals comprise nine Macaca fascicularis and two M. mulatta, aged 5-23 years. Table 1 provides sex, age, injection number and survival per animal, but site, assay-specific sampling and raw counts are unavailable. All three 23-year-old animals are male M. fascicularis.

BrdUrd was 75 mg/kg intraperitoneally, one to five injections separated by 24 hours. Five single-injection animals survived two hours; six animals with three or five injections survived one or two weeks after the last injection. One Results paragraph instead says after the first injection. This timing conflict remains unresolved.

Methods explicitly states that two hours permits S-phase labeling but not completed mitosis or migration. All three 23-year-old animals have only this two-hour interval. The reported oldest-age BrdU and TOAD-64 profiles do not establish birthdated neuronal differentiation at that age.

The modified optical fractionator uses coded slides and every twelfth 40-micrometre section, excluding the outermost focal plane. Estimates are not raw cell counts or instantaneous birth rates. Processed thickness, sampling implementation, raw stacks and animal-by-marker data are required for reproduction.

Table 1 gives dentate BrdUrd estimates of 4308, 3288, 1968, 2748, 1896, 1176, 780, 876, 420, 336 and 228 for animals 1-11. Mixed species, dose accumulation, age and survival prevent a pooled age-specific production rate. The single-dose two-hour age contrast has only one young and one middle-aged animal against three aged animals.

The neuronal-marker means concern the four five-injection animals 1, 3, 5 and 6: TOAD-64 1230.5 +/- 436.9, NSE 822.1 +/- 345.9 and calbindin 793.2 +/- 232.9. These are separate overlapping marker assays, not disjoint cell populations or universal fractions. NeuN is illustrated in animal 1; a complete quantified NeuN census is not supplied.

The PMC HTML Table 2 lists M. fascicularis group sizes of 4 young, 4 middle-aged and 2 aged, plus 2 middle-aged M. mulatta. These total 12 rather than the 11 Table 1 animals; Table 1 instead has 2 young and 3 aged animals. The reported F(2,5)=154.2 cannot be reproduced from an identified animal-level analysis. Printed-PDF agreement with the HTML table has not been verified.

TOAD-64 profiles indicate an immature neuronal phenotype under the marker assumptions. Figure 1F uses TOAD-64 and a DNA counterstain, not BrdUrd birth labeling. Its cells cannot be treated as an independently birthdated lineage or as an image from an aged animal; the caption identifies animal 1.

BrdUrd profiles in a region corresponding to the rodent rostral migratory stream, occasional mitotic figures and TOAD-64 profiles motivate an olfactory-neuron interpretation. They do not track movement to the olfactory bulb, common ancestry, arrival, synaptic integration or sensory function.

The abstract reports fewer new astroglial cells; the described neuronal examples lack GFAP. A complete GFAP count and animal-level fraction are not provided. Antibody-omission and confocal checks address staining artifacts, not a demonstrated founder lineage.

Cortisol, learning, stress, enrichment and functional circuit activity were not measured or manipulated. The discussion draws on other species and publications to propose survival, glucocorticoid and memory mechanisms. It does not supply matched primate causal evidence or a universal prerequisite.

This study and Kornack and Rakic (1999) use different doses, routes, survival schedules, marker assays and counting procedures. Agreement on some neuronal colabels does not make their numerical rates or age groups interchangeable. The reviewed 1985/1988 autoradiographic protocols differ in sampling and phenotype criteria; matched detection sensitivity remains unresolved.

studies.finding: Trace and place protocols increase previously labeled dentate-cell counts and reduce total pyknotic profiles. Other tasks and late-label counts retain null outcomes. Survival and functional necessity remain distinct mechanistic questions.
limitations: Adult male Sprague Dawley rats weighed 300-350 g; chronological age is not stated. Group sizes are generally five or six. The paper does not provide a complete animal manifest or randomized assignment procedure. Coded histology is reported, not complete blinding of every procedure.

BrdU was 200 mg/kg; the injection route is not specified. In the main experiments labeling occurred one week before four consecutive training days, with separate terminal cohorts 24 hours or seven days after training. The approximate three-week label-age wording does not exactly specify elapsed days. Separate sacrificed cohorts do not track individual cells longitudinally.

Trace conditioning used 200 trials per day for four days, an 83-dB 250-ms noise, a 500-ms gap and a 100-ms 0.7-mA shock. Unpaired rats received the same stimulus counts without explicit pairing. All paired animals reached 60% conditioned responses; none of the unpaired animals did. Complete naive-group electrode and handling matching is not specified.

Delay conditioning uses a 320-ms noise coterminating with an 80-ms shock and a different conditioned-response window. Trace and delay differ in stimulus durations and scoring as well as temporal gap. The reported F(1,19)=4.24, P=0.05 is called nonsignificant; this boundary result and final-day similarity are not statistical equivalence.

Place training uses a fixed submerged platform, cue training a visible platform moved among quadrants, with four trials per day for four days. Swim controls are yoked to place-training swim duration without a platform; their interval includes the omitted platform-rest time. Time matching does not establish identical stress, motivation or hormone exposure.

Hippocampal dependence is imported from prior lesion literature and, for the exact rat trace protocol, unpublished lesion data. No matched hippocampal lesion or selective newborn-cell manipulation is performed in this histology study. The graph links the specified task protocol to its measured outcome, not generic hippocampal necessity.

At 24 hours after training, prelabelled dentate BrdU counts are elevated after trace conditioning (F(2,15)=137.40, P=0.0001) and place training (F(3,20)=266.40, P=0.0001); Figure 1b/f gives six rats per group. Exact endpoint means are not tabulated and have not been digitized. The abstract doubling language is not an exact universal multiplier or an edge weight.

Delay conditioning has no detected BrdU-count increase (F(2,12)=1.889, P=0.1936); cue training and time-yoked swimming also lack the reported place-training increase. Nonsignificance is neither equivalence nor absence of a smaller effect. These selected tasks and controls do not prove that all possible learning or stress is irrelevant.

The late-labeling trace cohort receives BrdU on the final training day after learning criterion, followed by tissue collection 24 hours later. F(2,13)=0.011, P=0.9892 concerns that retained-label count, not every phase of proliferation throughout training or a direct instantaneous mitotic rate.

Subgranular pyknotic profiles are defined morphologically, not by neuron-specific birthdated identity. Trace means are 220.0 +/- 41.9 naive, 81.8 +/- 24.3 paired and 214.8 +/- 46.5 unpaired; the printed F(3,15)=12.339, P=0.0007 gives a numerator degree of freedom inconsistent with three ordinary ANOVA groups. No corrected statistic is substituted.

Place-training pyknotic means are 208.7 +/- 30.9 naive, 50.0 +/- 8.4 place, 222.0 +/- 48.1 cue and 236.0 +/- 34.2 swim, with reported F(3,20)=16.527, P=0.0001. The paragraph does not allocate these pyknotic counts unambiguously to the 24-hour or seven-day terminal cohorts. Reduced total pyknosis does not by itself identify survival of the BrdU-positive neuronal population.

BrdU-positive pyknotic profiles are rare, reported as 0-36 per dentate gyrus, and not observed after the two selected learning tasks. No BrdU-positive pyknotic profiles are observed in the 24-hour late-labeling cohort. These are detection-limited snapshots of labeled degeneration, not complete survival trajectories.

SVZ sampling excludes the anterior portion and uses sections spanning the dentate gyrus. The trace SVZ null is printed as F(2,15)=0.09 with P=0.3598, an inconsistent ordinary F-test pair. The maze SVZ null is F(3,20)=0.279, P=0.8538. Neither result establishes absence throughout the SVZ or brain.

Granule-cell-layer volume has no detected group difference in trace (F(2,15)=0.043, P=0.958) or maze (F(3,20)=0.302, P=0.8236) comparisons. Gross regional volume is not the count of newborn neurons, a measured replacement balance or an equivalence test.

The seven-day post-training groups are reported to retain elevated BrdU counts, without a separate endpoint figure, table or test. Marker proportions at that endpoint are approximately 57% TOAD-64, 11% GFAP and 71% calbindin among BrdU-labeled cells. Separate overlapping marker assays must not be summed into a cell-type partition.

Marker comparisons report F(3,20)=0.311, P=0.8169 for TOAD-64 and identical F(3,20)=0.572, P=0.6402 for GFAP and calbindin. Exact assay/cohort allocation and the duplicated statistics require raw data; they are not silently repaired. Minimum sampling is 50 labeled cells per animal on at least six sections, with confocal verification.

Counts use coded slides, every twelfth 40-micrometre coronal section and exclusion of the outermost focal plane. Pyknotic counts use the same modified optical fractionator; volume uses Cavalieri estimation. Processed thickness, raw counts, optical stacks and analysis code are unavailable. Statistical methods specify Neuman Keuls comparisons.

The control time course rises from two hours to one week and falls by two weeks after labeling, but involves separate terminal cohorts. The survival interpretation also draws on prior autoradiographic grain counts and unpublished observations. The authors explicitly cannot exclude proliferation; a unique survival mechanism is not experimentally isolated.

No newborn-cell necessity, selective rescue, synaptic-output or memory-storage test is performed. Untrained controls retain labeled cells, and the authors leave unspecified natural learning as a possible contributor to baseline survival. The study establishes neither a universal learning prerequisite nor its universal absence, and no primate or human generalization follows.

studies.finding: No heavily labeled adult neuronal profile was found under the stated sampling. Glial, endothelial and peripheral labeling was observed. Mixed ages, label thresholds and specimen overlap limit generalization.
limitations: Twelve rhesus monkeys were labeled at reported ages of six months to eleven years; Table 1 gives ages at death of seven months to seventeen years. This is a mixed developmental and adult sample, not twelve animals labeled after puberty. Age at death cannot substitute for age at injection.

One to seven injections of tritiated thymidine were given at 10 mCi/kg. This is radioactivity per body mass, not the later BrdU mass dose. The injection route is not stated. The narrative survival range is three days to more than six years; the table includes 6.3 years. Repeated exposures and long retention windows are not independent animals or instantaneous birth rates.

Table 1 describes six-digit dates as day/month/year, although entries such as 013183 require month/day/year. Under that interpretation case 11 ends with injection 011976 and death 012376, four elapsed days rather than the printed fourteen. Case 7 gives 043069 to 050269, two elapsed days versus three printed; inclusive dating may matter. The original dates and intervals remain unreconciled.

Between 500 and 1000 sections per animal were screened across major brain regions and spinal cord, followed by brightfield or Nomarski examination with a 63x oil objective. The estimated million cells per specimen is not an exact neuronal denominator, random whole-brain census or statistical upper bound on rare births. Table 1 specifies 8-micrometre sections and every second to tenth section depending on region size.

Heavy labeling was calibrated separately in each case from glial, endothelial or peripheral cells, usually more than 15-30 silver grains per nucleus. Light-microscopic autoradiography exposure was 12-18 weeks and electron-microscopic exposure exceeded 24 weeks. A common fixed threshold cannot be imposed retrospectively. Occasional neuronal profiles with fewer than five or six grains were not classified as newborn; artifact or DNA repair was proposed without a repair assay.

Nine animals were pregnant at injection; neuronal labeling in offspring served as a positive control. Peripheral renewing tissues were also examined. The offspring and tissue checks demonstrate label incorporation under their conditions; they do not establish complete sensitivity for rare adult neuronal births. Pregnancy and assay allocation by animal are unavailable.

Figure 1D-E and Figure 2 use a seven-month-old animal, with Figure 2 explicitly labeled at six months. These images are juvenile examples. Oligodendroglial labels were mostly reported at six and eighteen months, with only occasional postpubertal examples. Selected dentate GFAP and ultrastructural analysis is described without a complete case-by-assay manifest or independent neuronal-marker panel.

The memory and fixed-neuron-population interpretation has no behavioral, electrical, synaptic-output or selective neuron-replacement assay. The macaque null does not establish a general absence in humans or a necessary stable-neuron mechanism for memory.

Case identifiers and adult schedules in Eckenhoff and Rakic (1988) correspond to Table 1 death dates here. Publications and repeated injections cannot be counted as independent biological replications without reconciling specimen identity. The 1983 abstract and in-preparation work cited in reference 6 are not themselves the 1988 full article.

All three printed article pages 1054-1056, Table 1 and Figures 1-2 were read and visually inspected in the public ICTP-hosted reprint. The 1988 course cover is not the publication date. Original animal records, full assay allocation, raw sections and counts were not obtained or independently reproduced.

studies.correctionCheck: The primary PDF, PubMed/Europe PMC metadata and exact DOI correction, erratum and retraction searches were checked on 14 September 2026. No notice resolving the stated reporting conflicts was identified. This is not exhaustive correction surveillance.
studies.finding: Early neuronal-appearing labels and later nonneuronal profiles coexist with an adult neuronal-detection null. Repeated doses, shared specimens and separate phenotype assays cannot establish a universal cessation or memory mechanism.
limitations: Eighteen rhesus monkeys span E140 to seventeen years: seventeen receive autoradiography and one E144 animal is used only for electron-microscopic GFAP. Table 1 contains four adult animals aged five, ten, ten and seventeen years at collection. Their seven, three, five and one injections total sixteen exposures, not sixteen independent animals.

Methods specifies six early developmental animals with one intravenous 5-10 mCi/kg tritiated-thymidine injection and one-hour survival. Table 1 instead prints one day for these rows. The eleven additional animals are described as surviving five weeks to two years, while Table 1 includes fourteen days, three years and six years. No adult one-hour cohort is documented; early developmental sampling cannot supply an adult short-interval null.

For adult cases 112883, 012980, 012376 and 021583, ages, injection counts and survival correspond to Rakic (1985) cases 12, 10, 11 and 8. This is evidence of overlapping material, pending original identity confirmation. Shared juvenile identifiers also have discordant age/survival reporting: 030783 is P149-P184 here versus seven months at death in 1985; 031683 is P507-P549 and six weeks here versus nineteen months and thirty-five days. Neither independent pooling nor silent record merging is justified.

Left hemispheres were sectioned at 8 micrometres and exposed for 10-18 weeks. Heavy light-microscopic labeling is more than half the maximum grain count in the most intensely labeled cells of each case. Electron microscopy uses four nuclear grains under low-background conditions. These distinct assay thresholds must not be merged with each other or with the 1985 threshold.

GFAP immunochemistry uses 30-micrometre vibratome sections from five animals. Antibody penetration reaches only about three micrometres. The normal-goat-serum primary-antibody control is incubated at 4 degrees C, whereas primary antiserum incubation is at room temperature. A negative GFAP profile need not be a neuron; technical false negatives and other glial or precursor identities remain possible.

Postnatal short-interval and longer-survival groups contain different animals. Approximately 150 sections across three longer-survival ages yielded eight profiles classified morphologically as definitive granule neurons, only one in P90-P155. These are sampled profiles, not eight animals, a clonal lineage or a daily birth rate; Nissl morphology has acknowledged identity limits.

The P149-P184 interval is thirty-five days/five weeks in Table 1 and text, but Figure 4B says six weeks. Figure 5 uses P507-P549. Neither is an adult cohort. The five-year-old seven-injection animal has about two labeled profiles per ten sections at three months, all small SGZ profiles without typical neuronal morphology. The seventeen-year-old animal retains a label given six years earlier; collection age does not date a new division at seventeen.

GFAP composition in Figures 7-10 concerns small SGZ cells without birth-label selection. The E144 animal was never thymidine-labeled; about half its sampled small cells are GFAP-positive. Approximately 75% at six months and a majority at later ages do not quantify the astrocytic fraction of adult newborn cells or prove two founder lineages.

The combined electron-microscopic assay examined 120 ultrathin semiserial sections from selected areas in each of three animals aged six months, one and a half years, and five years. A dozen reliably radiolabeled cells were found, six GFAP-positive. This is a pooled three-age subset, not twelve adult neurons or a representative adult astrocyte fraction. Figure 11 is juvenile; Figure 12 is the five-year-old animal.

Figure 12B is described as an oligodendroglial type in Results but as resting microglia in the caption. Its specific subtype remains unresolved. No labeled profile had reported neuronal ultrastructure or synapses in the examined sections; this sampling-limited null does not prove absence of all neuronal precursor potential.

The discussion calls sixteen injections to four adult animals equivalent to independent labeling experiments. Repeated exposures share animals and cumulative label windows. The eleven-of-twelve-month coverage is also pooled across animals and ages, not a matched adult seasonal experiment. No formal rare-neuron detection bound or exact cessation age is calculated.

No lineage tracing identifies whether phenotypes arise from separate committed founders or a common multipotent founder. The discussion allows other glial lines, undifferentiated cells and potential neuronal differentiation under other conditions. Regional co-occurrence and GFAP phenotype cannot close a precursor-to-neuron construction rule.

Gliogenesis, replacement and stable-neuron memory roles are interpretations. No paired birth/death census identifies population feedback, and no functional or behavioral test establishes that neuron turnover impairs memory. The adult autoradiographic null remains distinct from a universal prohibition on adult neurogenesis.

All nineteen article pages, Materials and Methods, Table 1 and Figures 1-12 were read in the Europe PMC PDF; the table and all twelve figures were visually inspected. Original animal and section records, raw microscopy and quantitative analysis were not obtained or independently reproduced.

studies.finding: PV activation suppresses population cycle markers and PV inhibition increases them; tested SST/VIP manipulations retain nulls. Conditional gamma2 deletion changes early activation and later clone composition. Isolation retains an EdU difference under PV activation, while MCM2 housing contrasts are nonsignificant. Full feedback closure and exclusive mediation remain unresolved.
limitations: Adult mouse preparations use nestin-GFP, PV/SST/VIP-Cre and nestin-CreERT2;Z/EG lines with gamma2-floxed or control alleles. Sex and a complete group-specific animal manifest are not reported. Tamoxifen is a single 62 mg/kg intraperitoneal dose at 6-10 weeks. The Methods require at least four weeks after AAV surgery; schematic week labels do not supply exact ages for every animal.

Acute 300-micrometre slices were recorded at 32-34 degrees C, with RGL voltage clamp at -65 mV and 5 mM kynurenic acid. The internal solution is ambiguously printed as 135 mM CsCl gluconate. Clamp-current sign does not directly identify native membrane polarization, spiking or cell-cycle entry.

Main text, Online Methods and Supplementary Figure 1 print 200 mM for focal GABA/muscimol application; no micromolar substitution is made. Etomidate is 100 nM in the main text/Figure 1 but 10 micromolar in Methods. The etomidate dose remains unresolved, and pharmacological sensitivity does not establish receptor stoichiometry.

Population experiments use five consecutive days of stimulation, eight hours per day: ChR2 blue light at 472 nm, 5-ms pulses at 8 Hz for 30 seconds every five minutes, or continuous 593-nm eNpHR light. AAV volume, delivered light power and a full opsin-negative illumination control are not reported. No-light sham comparisons include the effects of the complete light protocol.

On day five, EdU is injected intraperitoneally at 41.1 mg/kg six times, two hours apart, with collection two hours after the last injection. Repeated injections are not independent replicates. EdU incorporation and MCM2 expression are cycle-related endpoints, not counts of completed neuronal differentiation, integrated neurons or an instantaneous birth rate.

Population scoring uses 40-micrometre sections, every sixth section, and nestin-positive inverted-Y morphology over an EdU- or MCM2-positive nucleus. Optogenetic counts are limited to one millimetre anterior and posterior to the injection. Densities per cubic millimetre and the MCM2-positive fraction have distinct denominators. Analyses are described as blinded; random assignment, raw unit records and multiplicity-adjusted tests are not supplied.

At two and seven days after induction, one GFP-positive RGL is classified as a quiescent clone and two or more nuclei as an activated clone. These are fixed-tissue, spatially assigned clones using a referenced method, not live observations of every division or independently verified common ancestry. Supplementary Figure 2d plots one dentate gyrus per dot; hemispheres and clones cannot automatically be treated as independent animals.

Gamma2 immunostaining is shown in RGLs, but Supplementary Figure 2f electrophysiology tests GFP-positive neurons at thirty days, not RGLs. Its seven-of-ten cKO response pattern is not a measured RGL deletion efficiency. Recombination can persist in descendants, so later survival or differentiation may contribute to clone composition.

Thirty-day Figure 3f and Supplementary Figure 3e use incompletely reconciled clone denominators: the supplementary pie categories omit single-R and no-R classes. N includes intermediate progenitors or neurons, not exclusively mature neurons. Exact class percentages must not be pooled or converted to transition probabilities.

The population diazepam protocol is 5 mg/kg intraperitoneally once daily for five days. The clonal drug comparison instead uses six daily doses after tamoxifen and analysis at seven days. Diazepam is systemic. Pairwise drug responses or nulls without a reported genotype-by-drug interaction do not isolate an exclusive cell-autonomous mediator.

Social isolation starts immediately after weaning and lasts at least six weeks before labeling. The two housing conditions are crossed with light versus sham; this is not a selective learning manipulation. PV activity and extracellular GABA are not measured as the intervening response to isolation in the same animals.

Figure 5c retains higher EdU-positive RGL density in isolated versus group-housed animals under PV light stimulation (reported P < 0.05). In that same housing comparison, MCM2-positive density and fraction are nonsignificant (P > 0.1). These endpoints do not support complete abolition of the isolation effect or equivalence; the light-treated group is also distinct from the untreated group-housed baseline.

Figure 4 population comparisons use three or four animals per condition; Figure 5c uses four. Reported Student t-tests do not provide an equivalence margin, complete unit manifest or a formal factorial interaction. SST/VIP nulls apply to the tested lines, protocols and readouts, not all possible interneuron functions.

No matched experiment follows physiological circuit demand through PV signaling, RGL division, newborn-neuron survival and functional integration to restoration of circuit output. Supplementary Figure 8 imports schematic connectivity proportions, not measured weights. A reported reconstruction covering over 200 RGLs is spatial coverage, not 200 verified functional contacts or a minimum carrier count. Movie legends were read; movie files and custom reconstruction code were not replayed.

All six main PDF pages, Figures 1-5, Online Methods and all nine supplementary PDF pages with Figures 1-8 and Movie 1-3 legends were reviewed. Raw animal-level data, microscopy, recordings, movie files and analysis code were not obtained or independently reproduced.

studies.finding: Sox2-labeled populations show expandable culture potential and neuronal, astroglial or Sox2-retaining phenotypes in distinct assays. Sparse mixed clusters support conditional common-founder and self-renewal interpretations. Running comparisons report increased cycle-related markers and nonsignificant GFP-density differences, but reporter-control identity is unresolved. Complete lineage cycles and population-maintenance mechanisms remain hypotheses.
limitations: The 5.5-kb Sox2-promoter GFP transgenic line 1F7 is distinct from the 3.1-kb Sox2-GFP/Cre viral cassette and ROSA26 GFP or beta-gal reporters. Initial histology uses six-week mice; supplementary IHC specifies six to nine weeks, whereas clonal tracing uses six-week to three-month ROSA26 mice. Sex and a complete assay-specific animal manifest are not reported.

Marker meaning depends on niche and morphology. SGZ radial processes express nestin, GFAP and BLBP; lack of somatic signal makes nonradial nestin/GFAP assessment infeasible, not a demonstrated negative phenotype. Hilar astrocytic and SVZ ependymal marker combinations cannot be assigned the SGZ stem-cell interpretation automatically.

FGF2/EGF growth conditions and FACS select an expandable culture population. The preparation pools four pairs of hippocampi; the complete independent culture/animal allocation is unavailable. Enrichment and serial passage do not measure in vivo self-renewal frequency or establish that every cultured cell preserves its original in vivo potential.

The seven-day 5-micromolar forskolin assay shows neuronal and astrocytic markers. RIP-positive oligodendroglial differentiation uses a separate coculture with P0 rat hippocampal neurons and a donor beta-gal label. These conditions do not show in vivo tripotency, functional myelination or all three fates and serial renewal in one fully documented founder lineage.

At seven days, the lentiviral control reports SOX2 in 70% of GFP-positive cells and NeuN-positive off-target labeling of 26 +/- 3%, with n=800 cells, not 800 animals. BrdU selection is used to exclude nondividing off-target neurons. Animal-level denominators, initial recombination timing and complete lineage specificity are not established by this endpoint control.

Population fate mapping uses 100 mg/kg BrdU daily for seven days, starting ten or twenty-eight days after lentivirus. Methods specifies collection four weeks after the last injection, while Figure 3A marks analyses at days thirty-eight and fifty-eight. These statements do not reconcile to one exact label-age schedule; the injection route is unspecified.

Table 1 uses separate immunostaining panels, so marker percentages are not a partition of one cohort. Its S-100beta row prints three positive cells among thirty-two and 6.1%; these disagree because 3/32 is 9.375%. Neither value is silently substituted, and exact pooled fate probabilities are not admitted.

Retroviral specificity is reported as 92 +/- 1.7% SOX2 colabeling at seven days in a separate n=3 control. Twenty-one-day lineage assignments rely on sparse labeling and proximity, without founder barcodes, live division trees or a reported chance-collision bound. Clusters and hemispheres are nested within twenty-seven animals.

Table 2 lists 301 neuron-only, seven astrocyte-only, ten Sox2-only, fifteen Sox2-plus-neuron, one neuron-plus-astrocyte and twenty-nine undetermined clusters, totaling 363 across fifty-four hemispheres. Homogeneous categories include one- and two-cell clusters. These are cluster counts, not independent animal counts or an unbiased lineage-fate probability distribution.

Figure S4 traverses optical depth in micrometres, not elapsed time. The radial-process example is a fixed mixed cluster, not observation of its founder or a conversion event. Figure 4D has differing GFP and beta-gal panel labels; reporter identity needs clarification before panel-specific quantitative reuse.

Running Methods specifies seven transgenic runners and seven wild-type littermate controls, but Figure 5 shows and counts GFP-positive cells in both groups. The main paper and supplement do not resolve this control-genotype conflict. A matched reporter-genotype intervention effect is therefore not admitted.

The comparison uses individual cages with or without wheel access, seven daily 100 mg/kg BrdU injections and collection twenty-four hours after the last injection; the route is unreported. Figure 5A and caption do not uniquely fix wheel-access duration. Accumulated BrdU, terminal Ki67 and DCX are different readouts, not completed neuron production or functional integration.

Figure 5 reports densities per million cubic micrometres. GFP is sampled across the dentate rostrocaudal axis, while other markers use four dorsal hippocampal sections. Supplementary histology uses forty-micrometre sections; the stated every-twelfth-section and 440-micrometre interval lack a spacing-reference convention. GFP counting is described as blind; full animal allocation, raw measurements and multiplicity-adjusted analyses are unavailable.

Reported GFP-density comparisons have P=0.1724, n=7 for total reporter cells and P=0.1125, n=5 for radial cells. These nonsignificant comparisons do not establish equivalence, conservation of whole-population counts or a constant pool through time. The control-genotype conflict also applies to these nulls.

Figure 6 models population maintenance and possible radial/nonradial lineage relations. Its caption explicitly distinguishes asymmetric contribution at population level from asymmetric division of individual cells. Birth, death, survival, marker kinetics and a regulated feedback variable are not jointly measured; no universal stem-cell minimum or closed homeostatic construction is established.

studies.finding: PF sample selectivity can reappear between distractors, while match enhancement and repetition suppression have different task dependence. These observations do not establish a causal local storage or PF-to-IT route.
limitations: Two rhesus monkeys supplied 264 screened PF units; 145 task-responsive units were retained (98 in the ABBA-trained animal and 47 in the standard-task animal). The other 109 units were not studied further. Cells are nested within two animals; this is not an unbiased PF prevalence estimate. Sex and ages are unspecified.

The sample and test images last 500 ms with 1000-ms blank intervals and zero to four intervening nonmatches. ABBA trials repeat an irrelevant nonmatch; standard trials do not. Task/training differences are confounded with animal identity. PF visual responses use 90-290 ms after onset and delay activity the last 600 ms of each blank interval.

The text reports forty delay-selective units, including 33/98 ABBA and 7/47 standard units; Table 1 instead lists 32/98 for ABBA. Match-enhancement counts also differ across the text and table, with mixed response types. No exact reconciled subgroup prevalence or exclusive partition is admitted.

The 135 IT units were previously recorded in the ABBA animal and reanalyzed. They are not simultaneous paired PF-IT recordings or an independent replication. Figure 7 pools forty PF units across two animals against twenty-five IT units from one animal; selection and animal composition differ.

Best/worst-sample traces use selected neurons and sample rankings. Reported half-trial discriminant classification excludes the first delay and averages 20.8% versus six-way chance of 16.7%; the paper does not specify that unit selection was nested within training folds. No classification, multiplicity correction or neural minimum is independently reproduced.

PF feedback to IT is proposed in the Discussion. The authors explicitly state that the direct PF-deactivation test of IT match enhancement had not been tried. Response precedence, delay persistence and ramping do not identify an exclusive local recurrence, directed feedback route, accumulator or complete control circuit.

The measured ion has three trap modes. The free cyclotron frequency is reconstructed from their squared frequencies; the trap cyclotron mode alone is not the free frequency.
The paper writes omega_c=q*B/(m*c) in Gaussian units. In SI the expression is omega_c=abs(q)*B/m for the frequency magnitude; an angular frequency differs from cycles per second by 2*pi.

The ions are loaded and measured alternately, not simultaneously. Removing a fitted magnetic drift does not make all residuals or adjacent ratios statistically independent.

The boron gamma branching fraction and thin-target absorption normalization cancel only with the stated common detector response and loss corrections. Omega here is a fraction of 4*pi; illuminated alpha-detector area is assumed fully efficient. R_Pu denotes total alpha emission from the source, including its minor 240Pu/241Am contributions, not a separately isolated pure-239Pu decay rate.

The idealized epsilon_0(0,0) is the monitor counting efficiency for an infinitesimally narrow beam striking the deposit center at the 2200 m/s reference speed. Conversion from the monochromatic response uses lambda_0/lambda_mono under the inverse-velocity assumption. Finite beam profile, target absorption and self-shielding corrections separate this quantity from an uncorrected measured count ratio. Both alpha and triton capture products contribute; this is not a neutron survival probability.

The thesis and detailed article describe the calibration associated with the earlier beam-lifetime monitor, not new neutron-lifetime acquisitions. The thesis Table 7.1 lists 27 runs from June-December 2010; the 2018 text repeats that range, while Figure 22 includes a March 2011 point. The exact mapping of runs, ancillary measurements and revised analysis across the 2011 thesis, 2013 lifetime update and 2018 article remains unresolved.

The thesis uses two spacer configurations and the Cu-Cu-1 aperture, diameter 25.6725+/-0.0030 mm. The 2018 article reports a nickel-coated copper aperture of 25.765192+/-0.000240 mm and source distance 87.4226+/-0.0015 mm, with different alpha rates and activity. Their reported source calibrations cannot be substituted or averaged as independent determinations of an identically specified preparation. No cross-version correction or physical source-aging estimate is established.

The 2018 article reports the corrected alpha count rate 125.740 per second and effective Omega_stack=0.0053415, followed by R_Pu=23538.4 per second. Their printed central quotient is 23540.204... per second, and display-rounding intervals do not include the reported activity center. Additional input or correction reconciliation is unresolved. This is a failure to reconstruct the printed result from those displayed inputs, not evidence that the experimental numerical analysis is wrong.

The beam analysis uses timed beam-on minus beam-off rates, the geometric mean of top and bottom gamma-detector rates, and thin-target/thick-target/thin-target cycles to suppress first-order gamma-efficiency drift. Gamma backgrounds, thresholds, pulse pileup, dead time and silicon-capture contributions remain explicit corrections; a count-rate ratio is not a raw absolute neutron count.

Within-campaign gamma-detector drift controls are distinct from the long-term 6Li-deposit and aperture stability assumptions needed to transfer a later calibration to the 2000-2001 lifetime acquisition. The thesis Chapter 8 treated that transfer as unresolved; the separately reviewed 2013 update adopts its stated temporal-stability model. No deposit-loss posterior or historical transfer is independently reproduced here.

Cancellation of nuclear normalization inputs in the ideal rate identity does not eliminate nuclear data from every correction. The detailed article uses neutron scattering/absorption inputs, radiative-capture cross sections, material attenuation and modeled neutron/gamma transport. Its remaining upstream nuclear data, image records and simulation implementations are not independently reproduced.

The wavelength is inferred from silicon Bragg measurements on the same beam, including a lambda/2 component correction. Unexplained angle excursions are retained and the wavelength uncertainty uses a conservative observed spread, rather than only the uncertainty of the weighted centroid. The wavelength fit and transport simulations are not replayed.

The 27 reported calibration points span three collimations and two gamma detectors with common and configuration-specific corrections. The article describes Gaussian variation of correction inputs followed by weighted constant fits. These points, detector channels and publications do not supply independent replications of the calibration standard; full correction covariance, exact grouping and analysis code are not recovered from printed tables.

Equation 28 in the 2018 article omits the factor 1/2 required to invert Equation 12, which counts both alpha and triton products. Equation 26 defines phi_abs as an absorbed fraction near 0.01016, but the later text labels the transmission correction 0.989846 as phi_abs. These printed formula/notation conflicts are retained; no claim is made that the numerical implementation followed them.

The thesis reports epsilon_0^AG=(3.1116+/-0.0016)e-5, the 2013 lifetime paper uses (3.1098+/-0.0017)e-5, and the detailed 2018 article reports idealized epsilon_0(0,0)=(3.1101+/-0.0018)e-5. Source-specific normalization, metrology, corrections and aggregation must be reconciled before substitution. No new lifetime is calculated from the 2018 value and these reports are not averaged.

Alpha-source activity, monitor count efficiency and a neutron-decay lifetime are different quantities. None establishes nucleon formation, eternal proton stability, a universal constituent minimum or a unique explanation of beam/bottle differences.

studies.finding: Nine non-input hadron masses per normalization set agree with the paper's comparison within the reported uncertainty; nucleon results are isospin symmetric. Two lightest rho/Delta channel points cannot supply a reliable mass extraction and are omitted.
limitations: The physical pion mass is reached by extrapolation from a minimum simulated mass of 190 MeV, not by direct simulation at the physical light-quark masses. Three finite lattice spacings support a specified continuum fit, not exact continuum dynamics.

Table S1 has fourteen base parameter rows, including auxiliary volumes for one row and paired strange masses for four rows. Those additional runs must not be collapsed into fourteen identical ensembles or counted as independent full-spectrum replications.

Analysis uses every tenth trajectory and up to eight source timeslices per configuration. Autocorrelation and binning diagnostics, including the long 10000- and 4500-trajectory runs, support the stated sampling; source timeslices do not supply independent simulations.
Spatial extents reach about 4 fm and temporal extents about 8 fm. M_pi*L around four is a finite-volume rule of thumb tested within this analysis, not a universal stability or carrier threshold.

The detailed action and hadronic operators are delegated to cited method papers. This graph records the reported setup without claiming a complete action implementation or independent numerical reproduction.

Gaussian sources and sinks of radius about 0.32 fm on Coulomb-gauge-fixed configurations show reduced excited-state contamination relative to point sources in Figure S1. Reduced contamination is not its exact elimination.
The twelve channels are pi, K, rho, K*, N, Lambda, Sigma, Xi, Delta, Sigma*, Xi* and Omega. N denotes the isospin-symmetric nucleon channel, not separately resolved proton and neutron masses.
The published effective-mass plots and finite-lattice fits are reported computational outputs. Underlying correlators, full covariance matrices and the numerical fitting pipeline are not reproduced.

Pion, kaon and Xi are inputs in the Xi set; pion, kaon and Omega are inputs in the Omega set. The twelve channels yield nine predictions per set. Both sets reuse the same ensembles and do not independently replicate one another.

The mass and continuum extrapolations are correlated. Two normalization methods, two chiral/Taylor strategies, three pion-mass ranges, two continuum forms linear in a or a^2, and eighteen time windows produce 432 analysis variants per hadron in each normalization set, not 432 experiments.

The central value is the fit-quality-weighted distribution median. The central 68% interval of that variant distribution estimates systematic uncertainty; 2000 bootstrap datasets supply the median distribution and its central 68% statistical interval. Statistical and systematic errors are combined in quadrature for final plotted bars.

The fit family estimates selected extrapolation and excited-state effects. Exact fit-quality weights, raw correlators, full covariances and independent fit replay are unavailable here; the paper's description of blind analysis does not establish a separately audited outcome-masking protocol.

Finite-volume image corrections use M_X(L)=M_X+c_X(M_pi)*exp(-M_pi*L)/(M_pi*L)^(3/2), with volume scans at about a=0.125 fm and M_pi=320 MeV. Resonance corrections additionally use a scattering model; no precise width determination is supplied.

The lightest pion-mass point at a about 0.085 fm is excluded for rho and Delta because the lowest level is dominated by a two-particle state and weakly sensitive to the resonance mass. All other mass-range cuts remain part of the analysis.

Table S2 fractions are correlated, non-Gaussian and averaged across Xi/Omega sets. Finite-volume terms are treated as corrections. The fractions must not be summed or normalized as independent probabilities or independent variances.

The comparison uses the paper's PDG 2006 isospin averages. QED and isospin breaking are absent; leading pion/kaon electromagnetic adjustments and the neglected residual effects remain approximations. The result does not resolve the proton-neutron mass difference.

A mass spectrum does not establish stability against weak decay, a neutron lifetime, a real-time hadron formation path, a universal three-constituent minimum, nuclear stability or downward causation. The introductory percentages about visible matter and mass origin are not calculated decompositions in this study.

Figure 3 shaded bands represent experimental decay widths, not mass-measurement uncertainties. Input symbols have no error bars because their values set model parameters; this is not evidence of exact independent prediction.

The excluded cases are rho and Delta at the lightest pion-mass point at a about 0.085 fm. They are a sensitivity failure of the selected lowest-energy readout, not evidence that the resonances or their interactions are absent.
Extracting a resonance mass from those lowest levels would need precise width information. The authors omit these cases to avoid using an experimental width as an extra mass-inference input.

The remaining fits infer masses and couplings across the simulated volumes and masses; their width sensitivity is limited and errors are large. Multiple levels and cross-correlators for precise widths are outside this paper.
This limitation belongs to the same simulation data as the spectrum. It is neither an independent experiment nor an intervention that removes a hadron or changes a fundamental rule.

limitations: The combined 2017/2018 dataset counts about 38 million surviving UCN, not 38 million beta decays or independently replicated lifetime measurements. The count is not separately assigned to each year.

The 5.5 T polarizer and spin flipper prepare low-field-seeking UCN for an NdFeB Halbach trap with a 60-120 G holding field. Transport energies up to about 180 neV, cleaning near 38 neV and the reported 50 cm/about 51 neV trap boundary refer to different stages.

The primary detector uses boron-10 capture in ZnS scintillator and two-PMT photon coincidences. Background, dead time, pileup and delayed scintillation affect the count; photoelectrons and neutron captures are different counting domains.

Three analyses share these acquisitions. They initially develop separately, compare run-level quantities after sharing blinded fits, and unblind when fitted lifetimes agree within 0.1 s. The timing shift is within a stated +/-15 s window; this is not three independent experiments.

Monitor weighting, spectral normalization and background estimates vary among analyzers and time subsets. Table I prints analysis-C intervals ((m-1)*t_fill,m*t_fill) without a division into twenty within-fill bins; the printed mean-arrival integral also lacks the normalization needed for count-rate input. These expressions require clarification before literal replay.

Original timestamps, detector corrections, regression coefficients, selection decisions, full nuisance-parameter covariance and numerical fitting implementations have not been independently reproduced.
The aluminum-exposed subset accounts for about 34% of the combined 2017/2018 data, not 34% of every year. The reported material-loss correction must remain part of the final lifetime interpretation.

The A/B/C estimates share acquisition and differ in selection, coincidence construction, normalization and background. Their statistical errors are correlated and must not be reduced by treating them as independent experiments.

Paired short/long yields and global fits are alternative analyses of these acquisitions. Global A uses Poisson counts and nuisance marginalization, B uses a quasi-Poisson/profile likelihood, and C uses yield chi-square with variance scaling; no unique raw fit is reproduced.
Loss corrections include the affected 2017 aluminum subset, residual gas, depolarization, incomplete cleaning and heating. The paired and global estimates already include their declared corrections.

A fitted lifetime in the hundreds of seconds limits an unqualified permanence claim for free neutrons within the model; it does not test bound-neutron nuclear stability or determine a quark constituent count.

Use the unweighted mean of the three full-data global central estimates and the largest statistical error, 0.28 s. The 2021 publication does not use an error-of-the-mean reduction or the later paper's yearly error-average rule.

The original systematic budget is +0.22/-0.16 s: event definition 0.13, normalization 0.06, depolarization +0.07, uncleaned +0.11, heating +0.08, aluminum 0.05 and gas 0.06 s. The nonzero central corrections +0.06 for aluminum and +0.11 for gas have already entered the reported lifetime.
The aluminum model estimates loss per encounter (2+/-1)*10^-4 and gives +0.15+/-0.07 s for the contaminated subset; its +0.06+/-0.05 s contribution to the combined result has a different scope.

The current result combines 2020, 2021 and 2022 with error-weighted yearly estimates; 2017 and 2018 are not new acquisitions in this combination.
